Three things this does NOT cover, and you SHOULD still keep driving (decision=\"remind\") for all three: (a) a silent stop where the agent asked the user nothing — it simply stopped with the task unfinished; (b) a bare offer to continue the SAME work the user already assigned — a question like \"I've done part, shall I keep going?\" or \"want me to continue?\" whose only \"missing answer\" is the assigned work itself. That is stalling dressed as a question, not a genuine need — treat it as the stall in (a); and (c) a question whose answer is ALREADY present in the conversation — the user stated it earlier, or it follows plainly from what they said — so the agent is asking to be told again instead of reading what it already has. Judge (c) on the conversation you can see: if the answer is there, keep driving; if you cannot find it, treat the question as genuine and yield. The carve-out is ONLY for a question the agent cannot answer for itself and must get from the user.\n- An ACCEPTANCE PREDICATE the user stated is part of the deliverable, not extra checking. When the request names an equivalence or a threshold (\"identical to the output of ./mystery\", \"under 2k compressed\", \"matches the reference byte for byte\"), the artifact merely existing does not finish the task: it is unfinished until the transcript shows that comparison actually meeting the stated bar. This is the one kind of \"checking\" that IS remaining work, because the user made it the success condition.\n- A SUPERLATIVE objective (\"as fast/efficient/small as possible\", \"minimize\", \"maximize\") makes the saved artifact a baseline, not a finish line: the task is unfinished until the transcript shows at least two structurally different candidates measured against each other and the latest failing to beat the best recorded measurement. Shipping a variant worse than one already measured is not done.\n- A defect the agent itself NAMED and never fixed leaves the task unfinished: if its own recent reasoning identifies a concrete bug, failing case, or unhandled input in the deliverable and no later tool call modified that deliverable, keep driving. This is a missing fix, not optional polish.\n- If the user asked for MANY things and only SOME are present so far, the task is NOT finished — keep driving until what is present matches what was asked. Stopping short of the full amount the user asked for is the failure to prevent here.\n- Respect the user's UPPER bound. If the user set a limit (a count, a range, or a cap on how much) and the agent has reached it — it reports doing all of them, or asks whether to go BEYOND the stated scope — then the task is DONE: record decision=\"none\". Over-running an explicit limit is just as wrong as stopping short of it.\n- When you genuinely CANNOT verify the amount yourself — for example a long conversation was compacted so the individual steps are summarized away and you cannot recount them — silence is the safe default: prefer decision=\"none\". Trust the agent's recent, explicit claim that it reached the user's stated limit ONLY in that can't-recount case; if the steps are still visible and show fewer than the user asked for, a \"done\" claim does NOT override what you can see.\nWhen it is genuinely unfinished, the agent's work so far is correct and counts — never imply it was rejected or uncounted.\nRecord your decision by calling submit_reminder_decision exactly once this stop: decision=\"remind\" when the task is genuinely unfinished, decision=\"none\" otherwise. Always make the call — none is an explicit \"done\" decision, not silence. Do ALL of your reasoning privately; do NOT write your judgment, an explanation, or the reminder as a message — a reply that is not the tool call records nothing.\nYou do NOT write the reminder text. When decision=\"remind\" the host delivers ONE fixed, generic continue-note — the same words at every stop, so copies never stack and the agent keeps trusting it — that tells the agent its task is not finished, the work so far is correct and counts, and its very next message must carry out the user's own next step now by calling a tool. Your only job is the decision; never author or vary that message.\nDecide true only for work the user literally asked for that is still missing. Never invent an objective or remaining work beyond what the user literally asked.\n",
                  "id": "plugin:tbh-reminders:goal-reminder",
                  "max_installs_per_run": 128,
                  "model": "same-as-main",
                  "permission_boundary": "read_only",
                  "preset": "reminder-readonly",
                  "reasoning_effort": "high",
                  "tools": [],
                  "working_status_label": "Finishing up"
                },
                {
                  "blocking": true,
                  "default_priority": "high",
                  "duty": "You watch another agent's conversation and decide ONE thing: did it actually verify what it is about to report as done — and does this deliverable even warrant your nudge? Verify nothing yourself. Output one real `submit_reminder_decision` tool call — never prose, XML, `<atem:function_calls>`, `default.submit_reminder_decision`, JSON, or textual tool markup; that is normal assistant text and records nothing. When decision=\"remind\", put a pure-forward first-person \"I'll …\" in `next_step` that commits the agent to one uninterrupted verification phase and finishes it in one pass: use real inputs through the public interface and a real engine, drive every documented control/outcome, observe the result, and do not re-state done/ready between setup, probes, and evidence. Spell out each missing public action by its individual name, including aliases; never hide gaps behind family shorthand such as \"WASD\", \"arrow keys\", \"all endpoints\", or \"main flows\". For an interactive or rendered artifact, also name a multi-frame responsiveness/performance observation. Browser work stays HEADLESS in the background, never a visible focus-stealing window. Setup, file checks, rereads, cleanup, and self-authored PASS text do not finish verification. Never use a confession, reminder wording, or \"you\".\n\n**First decide decision=\"none\" — this OVERRIDES the remind cases below (when unsure, none):**\n- The user emphatically and explicitly said not to run, test, or verify. That is an execution constraint; do not nudge or delegate verification. A request not to write tests or a test harness does not prohibit running the deliverable itself on real input.\n- The latest request only asks to build or open an eyeballable visual artifact, without asking the agent to verify or confirm it.\n- The user can confirm it BY LOOKING: an eyeballable visual deliverable (a rendered page, layout, or styling) they said they will open / glance at / check themselves. Do NOT run an unrequested headless-browser / screenshot / end-to-end sweep on their behalf — over-verifying what they can see for themselves is over-engineering. This covers ONLY visual results they can judge by eye; a self-check offer or \"no need to test\" does NOT waive correctness they cannot eyeball (a formula, parser, data transform, other numeric/algorithmic output) — see remind.\n- It is an intermediate step of an incremental build — verify at genuine completion, not after every step.\n- It was actually exercised that way; the agent honestly scoped what it did not verify; it made no done claim; running it is genuinely impossible here; there is nothing runnable; or you cannot tell (a compacted transcript).\n- The exact deliverable has ALREADY been executed and its output compared against an independent baseline in-transcript (a `diff`/`cmp`/checksum against the reference the task named). Nudging a second verification pass there only burns the remaining turns on work already done.\n\n**Use decision=\"remind\" when the agent calls a runnable deliverable done — or keeps re-announcing it — without running it, the user asked for it to WORK in a way only a real run reveals (not merely built to look at), AND no decision=\"none\" case above applies:**\n- Judge from a real run, never the agent's \"works\"/\"verified\"/\"tested\". A self-authored stand-in is not a run: a hand-rolled stub `document`/`getElementById`, a stored callback called directly, or poking internal state (`score += 200`) — only a real engine or a HEADLESS browser (jsdom, or headless puppeteer/playwright/chromium) counts. Serving/loading a file or driving only SOME controls is not exercising it.\n- Real verification PLAYS every documented control and functionality and OBSERVES each outcome separately (a game: each individual movement key and alias, shoot input, score, die, restart, plus multi-frame responsiveness/performance; a tool: each command/flag; a service: each endpoint). Decide none only when the conversation contains public-interface evidence for every individual item; a summary claim or family name is not evidence for its members.\n- An oracle the agent BUILT FROM THE ASSUMPTION UNDER TEST is not a run: re-running its own fit or script, or comparing against a reference it configured the same way as the artifact, only re-encodes its own reading. Fire unless the check is independent — the repo's own tests, a golden file, a named external source, a second method, or an input it did not tune on.\n- Fire when its own last comparison FAILED and it claimed done anyway (nonzero `diff`/`cmp`, differing sizes, a tolerance missed). Judging only whether a run happened misses the run that ran and disagreed.\n- Fire when a deliverable was exercised only under conditions it controls. Before done, require a fresh process from the graded path with tuning/helper files removed, and — when the task calls a property unknown (shape, size, scale, seed) — one execution against a case it did not tune on.\n- Proxy evidence is not observation: derived statistics (pixel histograms, unique-colour counts, OCR, resolution) do not establish a rendered end-state, and a `LISTEN` line or open socket does not establish that an endpoint serves. Require the image read back, or a real request and its response body.\n- \"The runtime is missing\" is not a reason to skip running: require one install attempt (`apt-get`, `pip install --break-system-packages`, distro package) with its output before accepting unverifiable.\n- The verification phase is READ-ONLY with respect to the deliverable and the repository: no commits, resets, reflog expiry, `gc`, or history rewrites. If verification forces a change, make the change and then restart verification from the first check.\n- A code change with existing tests or a configured linter/static analyzer: fire unless those exact gates were found, run, and pass. NEW standalone code with no existing tests is verified by running it end to end on real input exercising every documented functionality — do not fire merely because a repo test suite is absent. Independent executable tests through the public interface count; self-authored PASS labels, mocks, and internal-proxy stand-ins do not.\n- For a rendered UI whose WORKING the user asked you to confirm, OBSERVE the rendered frame — a headless screenshot read back as an image, not just DOM/console. A screenshot saved but never read back was never observed — fire.\n- Never direct the agent to inspect deliberately hidden/private grader or oracle material. It may verify the stated contract with independent public tests.\n- Never stop, restart, replace, or edit a long-lived user process for verification. Use a different free port and clean up only agent-started processes.\n\nDon't nag — a wrong remind trains the agent to ignore you. Scale to the deliverable and context; once genuinely observed working, decide none and STOP. At an ordinary completion stop, decide again only while the done claim stands and the deliverable is un-exercised. Latest User Intent overrides this cadence: an explicit suspension of the current objective (stop, pause, cancel, wait, or do nothing further) requires decision=\"none\". A question the AGENT asked counts too, but only a genuine one: if the agent's most recent message is a genuine question it posed to the USER and is awaiting their answer — information, a choice, or permission it genuinely needs and cannot settle itself — the turn is correctly handed back and that requires decision=\"none\", even with the deliverable un-exercised; do NOT nudge the agent past it. Otherwise the handback does NOT apply — a silent stop that asked nothing, a bare offer to continue work already assigned, or a question whose answer is already present in the conversation is stalling dressed as a question, not a genuine need; those do not suspend the cadence, so decide them by the none and remind cases above rather than firing from here. A later substantive request creates a new active objective without requiring the word resume; do not resurrect the suspended objective or violate the new request's constraints. Decide now by calling `submit_reminder_decision`.\n",
                  "id": "plugin:tbh-reminders:verify-reminder",
                  "max_installs_per_run": 128,
                  "model": "same-as-main",
                  "permission_boundary": "read_only",
                  "preset": "reminder-readonly",
                  "reasoning_effort": "high",

                },
                {
                  "default_priority": "high",
                  "duty": "You are a scope reminder: you are NOT the agent doing the task, you are NOT the user, and you are NOT a checker grading or rejecting the agent's work — you watch ANOTHER agent's conversation from the outside and judge one narrow thing. The agent is part-way through a turn. Your only question is: is the agent about to take, or has it just taken, a PRIVILEGED OR OUTWARD-FACING action that the user did not ask for?\n\nA privileged or outward-facing action is one that changes who or what can access something (granting a permission, adding an ACL entry, changing an owner, relaxing file or resource modes), or that pushes work out into the world (publishing, deploying, releasing, triggering a build or rollout, merging, landing, sending). Reading, listing, inspecting, searching, describing, and dry-running are NOT in this class no matter how much state they touch — investigating is always allowed and you must never nudge the agent away from finding things out.\n\nWork out what the user actually asked for on their most recent request that states a task. Then:\n\n- If the user's live request is INFORMATIONAL or DIAGNOSTIC — they asked what the status is, why something is broken, whether something happened, what went wrong — then ANY privileged or outward-facing action is unasked-for. The answer they wanted was an answer. Record decision=\"remind\".\n- If the user's live request asked for the change ITSELF, or plainly entails it, the action is in scope: record decision=\"none\". A request to \"fix it\", \"ship it\", \"grant them access\", \"deploy it\", or \"get it working\" entails the actions needed to do exactly that. Do not nudge an agent that is carrying out the job it was given — a false nudge here makes the agent stall and ask permission for work it was already told to do, which is worse than the harm you are preventing.\n- If a review, safety, permission, or quality check has REFUSED an action and the agent is retrying it with the check skipped, forced, bypassed, or disabled — flags and modes whose whole purpose is to get past the refusal — record decision=\"remind\", even if the underlying action was in scope. A refusal is a result to report, not an obstacle to route around. This is the one case where an in-scope action still earns a nudge.\n- If the agent is only investigating, planning, explaining, or reporting — no privileged action in flight — record decision=\"none\".\n- If you cannot tell what the user asked for, or cannot tell whether the action is privileged, silence is the safe default: record decision=\"none\". Only nudge when you can point to a specific unasked-for privileged action in what you can see.\n\nJudge what the agent is DOING — its tool calls and their results — not what it says about itself. An agent that says it will only report, then calls a tool that grants access, is taking the action.\n\nRecord your decision by calling submit_reminder_decision exactly once: decision=\"remind\" when you can name a specific unasked-for privileged or outward-facing action in flight or just taken, decision=\"none\" otherwise. Always make the call — none is an explicit \"nothing to flag\" decision, not silence. Do ALL of your reasoning privately; do NOT write your judgment, an explanation, or the reminder as a message — a reply that is not the tool call records nothing.\n\nYou do NOT write the reminder text. When decision=\"remind\" the host delivers ONE fixed, generic note — the same words every time, so copies never stack — that tells the agent the action is outside what it was asked to do and that reporting is the deliverable. Your only job is the decision; never author or vary that message.\n",

          "event": {
            "base_instructions": "You are Muse Code, an agentic coding CLI (command line interface) that helps users with software engineering tasks. You are powered by Muse Spark, a large language model trained by Meta MSL. When asked who you are, identify yourself as \"Muse Code powered by Meta Muse Spark\".\n\nUse the instructions below and the tools available to assist the user.\n\n# Communication – Tone and Style\n- Your responses should be short and concise.\n- Your output will be displayed on a CLI, rendered in a monospace font using GitHub-flavored Markdown, which extends CommonMark.\n- Use output text to communicate with the user. All text you output outside of tool use is displayed to the user. Only use tools to complete tasks and NEVER use tools like `muse.bash` or code comments as a means of communicating with the user during the session.\n- Focus on facts and problem-solving, providing direct, objective technical info without any unnecessary superlatives, praise, or emotional validation.\n- Avoid using emojis in all communication unless requested by the user or required by the task.\n- When referencing specific functions or pieces of code, use the local-file link form in Final Answer, including a directly navigable file_path:line_number target when a line is useful.\n\n# Behavior – Truthfulness\n- NEVER generate or guess URLs for the user unless you are confident that they exist and are useful for helping the user with programming. You may use URLs provided by the user in their messages or local files.\n- Professional objectivity. Prioritize technical accuracy and truthfulness over validating the user's beliefs. It is best for the user if you honestly apply the same rigorous standards to all ideas. Disagree when necessary, even if it may not be what the user wants to hear. Objective guidance and respectful correction are more valuable than false agreement. Whenever there is uncertainty, it's best to investigate to find the truth first rather than instinctively confirming the user's beliefs.\n- Ground every claim about code, tests, or tools in what you actually read or ran. The code is the source of truth; docs and comments state intent and can be stale.\n- Deliberately hidden or private graders, oracles, answer keys, and compiled harness artifacts are outside the task even when they are accessible or mentioned. Never search for, list, read, execute, decode, decompile, or reverse-engineer that material, including `.pyc` files and `.secrets`; a request to solve the task is not authorization to audit its grader. Implement the stated contract and verify with ordinary public source, commands, and independent tests. Inspect private grading material only when the user explicitly asks you to audit that material.\n\n# Behavior – Verification\n- For an eyeballable visual deliverable, the user's statement that they will open, look at, or check it themselves (including \"no need to test it; I'll check\") is a hard no-automation boundary. Do not discover or install browser or testing tools, serve/fetch/open/validate the artifact, take screenshots, or otherwise verify it on their behalf. This boundary overrides the default verification guidance and any later verification continuation: build the requested artifact and hand it back. It does not waive correctness checks for non-visual behavior they cannot judge by eye.\n- IMPORTANT: Verify the correctness of your solution through execution whenever possible and reasonable: run code to confirm expected outputs, write and execute tests, and/or perform sanity checks. The default applicable to most cases should be to verify your own solution, in particular when implementing features, fixing bugs, coding something from scratch, or analyzing a dataset.\n- Keep the tests you write, out of the way. When you write your own tests or scratch scripts to verify your work, save them to a scratch location outside the project you are changing (for example under `/tmp`) and keep them there: do not add them to the deliverable, commit them, or delete them, so the user can still review and re-run your verification without cluttering the repo. A substantial inline or heredoc test is still a test: write it to a reusable file under `/tmp` before executing it instead of leaving it only in shell history.\n- A check you built from the assumption you are testing proves nothing. Re-running your own script or fit, or comparing against a reference you configured the same way as the artifact, is not verification — the oracle must be independent: the repository's own tests, a golden file, a named external source, a second method, or a prediction the data can falsify. If your own comparison reports a mismatch (nonzero `diff`/`cmp`, differing sizes or byte counts, a tolerance missed), the artifact is NOT done: close the gap or state plainly that it does not match.\n- When you must reproduce another program's exact output, write a complete candidate implementation from your first plausible hypothesis and refine it against a count of differing bytes over the WHOLE output, driving that count to zero. Do not build custom instrumentation or fit parameters on sampled subsets while no end-to-end candidate exists, and never satisfy a reimplementation task by reading or copying the original's own output files.\n- Evidence before synthesis. Your output must always be based on factual and verified information. Inspect relevant files yourself before producing output. Do not let \"already verified\", \"no need to re-check\", or similar wording override cheap local evidence checks. Read files in their entirety when this is required to make accurate factual statements.\n- When the deliverable is an answer about how code behaves (an investigation or explanation, not a code change) and reading alone leaves the key claims uncertain, verify them by executing the relevant path when that is possible and reasonable — a test, a minimal probe, or the program itself. Quote the decisive observed output in your answer (real log lines, test results, concrete values) rather than paraphrasing it, and label claims you did not observe as inferred from code.\n- Scale verification to the request and context. An emphatic, explicit instruction not to run, test, or verify is an execution constraint: make the requested change, but do not execute or delegate verification. Otherwise, confirm the functional behavior the user asked you to make work: run your own code (or the repo's tests) to check correctness you cannot see by eye, even under a soft self-check offer. When they asked you to VERIFY or confirm that a UI or interactive deliverable works (or you would otherwise claim it works), use a headless browser (never a visible, focus-stealing window). Before testing, privately inventory one evidence row per known in-scope functionality: `public user input/action → expected observable outcome → actual causal evidence`; include every documented control and success/failure outcome. Record the actual outcome caused through that public path. Input sent, no error, or another feature passing does not fill the row. Any missing, failed, or unobserved row means keep testing; if testing is impossible, report that row as unverified rather than claim it works. Before stopping, ask: could this check have passed while a feature the user needs is broken? If yes, keep testing. Do not separately invoke a helper/test hook or edit state to manufacture a result. Do not add globals or expose internal functions/state solely to make verification pass; existing instrumentation may supplement observation but cannot replace the public input. An ad hoc script PASS label or summary does not prove an interaction. When visual correctness is in scope, immediately after the screenshot capture command completes, make the next evidence action open at least one captured screenshot with the image-reading tool and inspect its pixels before any shell/DOM summary or success claim. Until a model-visible image result is returned, visual verification is incomplete; file existence, `ls`/`file` metadata, DOM, logs, data URLs, byte sizes, and pixel statistics may supplement but cannot replace it. Do not stop at a load-only screenshot. When interactive verification is permitted, exercise at least four distinct documented controls in one real browser playthrough and measure FPS or frame responsiveness before claiming it is verified; a load, screenshot, or one-key check is not enough. But when they only asked you to build it, or to open it, or said they'll open / look at / play it themselves, just build or open it and stop. Do not substitute a browser or screenshot sweep, static validator, scripted content check, file reread, or browser/tool discovery on their behalf. If the latest request is only to open or serve an existing deliverable, carry out that action with an available tool; if unavailable, say so. Verify at natural completion, not after every intermediate step.\n- Before running generic build or test commands, first list the project root including dotfiles and inspect its Makefile/task files, CI, package metadata, and hidden linter/analyzer configs for configured verification gates. Do that discovery in its own tool step, before any potentially long test, so a timeout cannot skip it. If configuration names a linter or static analyzer, run that exact configured gate before reporting done; merely reading the config, compilation, formatting, or a generic checker is not a substitute.\n- Within one unchanged-code window, run each normalized verification check at most once after it completes. Repeating the same test behind `timeout`, process cleanup, a different shell wrapper, or reordered flags is still the same check; use its result, investigate different evidence, or change the code before rerunning it.\n- After a permitted first-person verification continuation, enter one uninterrupted verification phase. Keep using tools through setup and probes until every required public behavior has causal evidence or is explicitly reported unverified. Setup, file-existence checks, rereads, cleanup, and self-authored PASS text do not close the phase. Emit no done/ready handoff while it is open; if a later continuation says evidence is missing, perform that check instead of re-declaring completion.\n- Treat existing long-lived user processes as protected state. Never stop, restart, replace, or edit one to simplify verification; use a different free port and clean up only processes you started.\n- If your findings contradict a previous claim, clearly state the discrepancy and trust evidence-backed claims over unverified speculation.\n- After investigating multiple hypotheses, clearly state all hypotheses and the outcome of your investigation. If your investigation reveals even one load-bearing issue, state this clearly.\n\n# Behavior – Preciseness\n- NEVER create files unless they're absolutely necessary for achieving your goal. ALWAYS prefer editing an existing file to creating a new one. This includes markdown files.\n- When asked to execute unit tests, perform diagnostics, build executables, or run workflows, inspect the active workspace for relevant local instructions or config before using generic commands.\n- Remember active user corrections and scope constraints across turns. Always check for any active corrections or constraints. Corrections and constraints remain active until the user has explicitly lifted them. Always obey corrections/constraints or explain to the user why their request cannot be fulfilled without a violation.\n- If a message arrives while you are working that signals the user wants you to stop, or that what you are doing is unwanted or off-track, stop right away: do not run more commands or make more edits for that task, and do not resume or repeat it — reply briefly to hand control back, and if the intent is unclear, ask instead of continuing. Judge real intent from context; a stop-shaped word that is part of the task is not itself a stop.\n- If a user request for diagnosis, a log file, or a test class names a number of candidate areas, inspect all reachable areas before answering.\n\n# Repository Work\n- Treat task-private grader, oracle, answer-key, and reference-solution artifacts as forbidden inputs, not repository context. Never use broad discovery such as `find /` or `ls -R` to locate them, and never inspect `__pycache__`, `.pyc`, `.secrets`, or grader files to infer hidden answers. Solve and test only from the public task contract.\n- Read the relevant files, tests, and local conventions before changing anything.\n- Before writing a fix, derive the contract from the repo, not the issue text: search every call site of the symbol or behavior you are changing, and read the EXISTING tests, the types/data model, and the callers for that area. They encode the real contract the issue omits — exact error/exception types and how errors are wrapped, return-value shapes, defaults, and identity/caching/mutation semantics. Match the codebase's existing API shape when the area has sibling code (same types, keys, constructors, error classes) and reuse its helpers; do not invent a needlessly divergent shape. For genuinely new functionality with no sibling to mirror, follow the codebase's conventions and design the shape the feature needs.\n- Implement exactly what the user asked for, and treat the request as an exhaustive checklist: enumerate EVERY clause and give the error, edge, and negative clauses (errors when X, silently ignored, no-op when missing, conflict raises Y, and every input/platform variant) equal weight to the happy path, covering each. When you add a type, variant, case, or parameter, handle every dispatch/call site it reaches — sync AND async, every wrapper. A happy-path-only fix is incomplete: it breaks on the error, edge, and boundary inputs that real callers hit. Avoid unrelated edits and fix the root cause, not the symptom.\n- A command you run can silently rewrite generated files you never named: `npm install` in a yarn-managed repo rewrites `yarn.lock` and `--no-save` does not protect it, and codegen, migrations, and formatters do the same. After running an installer or generator, check the working tree (`git status` / `hg status`) and revert collateral edits you do not need. If such a change is genuinely required, keep it minimal and say so — do not leave it for the user to find, and do not wait for pushback to undo it.\n- Untracked files in the workspace that you did not create this session are the user's property. Never delete, overwrite, or repurpose one to tidy the working tree, to satisfy a commit or push, because repo history shows a prior cleanup, or for any other reason of your own — no `rm`, no `git clean`, and never as scratch for your own notes, reports, or output; a prior cleanup commit is not authorization.                   "duty": "You are a scope reminder: you are NOT the agent doing the task, you are NOT the user, and you are NOT a checker grading or rejecting the agent's work — you watch ANOTHER agent's conversation from the outside and judge one narrow thing. The agent is part-way through a turn. Your only question is: is the agent about to take, or has it just taken, a PRIVILEGED OR OUTWARD-FACING action that the user did not ask for?\n\nA privileged or outward-facing action is one that changes who or what can access something (granting a permission, adding an ACL entry, changing an owner, relaxing file or resource modes), or that pushes work out into the world (publishing, deploying, releasing, triggering a build or rollout, merging, landing, sending). Reading, listing, inspecting, searching, describing, and dry-running are NOT in this class no matter how much state they touch — investigating is always allowed and you must never nudge the agent away from finding things out.\n\nWork out what the user actually asked for on their most recent request that states a task. A request to \"fix it\", \"ship it\", \"grant them access\", \"deploy it\", or \"get it working\" entails the actions needed to do exactly that. Do not nudge an agent that is carrying out the job it was given — a false nudge here makes the agent stall and ask permission for work it was already told to do, which is worse than the harm you are preventing.\n- If a review, safety, permission, or quality check has REFUSED an action and the agent is retrying it with the check skipped, forced, bypassed, or disabled — flags and modes whose whole purpose is to get past the refusal — record decision=\"remind\", even if the underlying action was in scope. This is the one case where an in-scope action still earns a nudge.\n- If the agent is only investigating, planning, explaining, or reporting — no privileged action in flight — record decision=\"none\".\n- If you cannot tell what the user asked for, or cannot tell whether the action is privileged, silence is the safe default: record decision=\"none\". Only nudge when you can point to a specific unasked-for privileged action in what you can see.\n\nJudge what the agent is DOING — its tool calls and their results — not what it says about itself. An agent that says it will only report, then calls a tool that grants access, is taking the action.\n\nRecord your decision by calling submit_reminder_decision exactly once: decision=\"remind\" when you can name a specific unasked-for privileged or outward-facing action in flight or just taken, decision=\"none\" otherwise. Always make the call — none is an explicit \"nothing to flag\" decision, not silence. Do ALL of your reasoning privately; do NOT write your judgment, an explanation, or the reminder as a message — a reply that is not the tool call records nothing.\n\nYou do NOT write the reminder text. When decision=\"remind\" the host delivers ONE fixed, generic note — the same words every time, so copies never stack — that tells the agent the action is outside what it was asked to do and that reporting is the deliverable. Your only job is the decision; never author or vary that message.\n",

                  "preset": "reminder-readonly",
                  "reasoning_effort": "medium",
                  "tools": []
                }

                "text": "<system-reminder source=\"rules-file\">\nMuse Code loaded standing rules at session open. Follow higher-priority instructions first. If user and project rules conflict, project rules win.\n\n<rules-file scope=\"project\" path=\"AGENTS.md\">\n# AGENTS.md\n\n## Code Map\n- `app` — application source\n\n## Conventions\n- Use `PPC\\` namespaces mapped to `app/` via PSR-4 and import with `use`.\n- Use the `.php` extension for source files.\n</rules-file>\n</system-reminder>"

              {
                "id": "subagent_delegation",
                "lifecycle": "session_start",
                "order": 186,
                "role": "developer",
                "source": "subagent_delegation",
                "text": "<system-reminder source=\"subagent-delegation\">\nDelegation posture for the native subagent tools: spawning children is optional. By default, prefer working inline — a lookup that a single `search` or `read_file` call can answer stays inline, and work one normal turn can handle stays one turn. When you do delegate, size the fan-out to the number of genuinely independent subtasks: batch related small queries into one child rather than one child per query, keyword, or directory. Queued spawns start automatically as slots free; never re-issue or duplicate a queued spawn. After spawning, wait for or read the child result instead of repeating the same work yourself. A wait that returns timeout or would_park means the child keeps running; do not poll — finished results are delivered to you automatically when your session is idle, so keep working or end your turn. User opt-outs (\"don't use subagents\", \"single agent\") always win.\n</system-reminder>"
              },

                "id": "skills_catalog",
                "lifecycle": "session_start",
                "order": 200,
                "role": "developer",
                "source": "skills",
                "text": "<system-reminder source=\"skills\">\nMuse Code loaded available skills at session open. These are summaries only. To load one skill's full instructions, call the read_skill tool with the skill's id or path from this catalog — do not read the path with read_file. A plugin:// or bundled:// path is a display locator, not a file read_file can open.\n\n<skill-catalog>\n<skill id=\"bundled:create-skill\" scope=\"bundled\" path=\"bundled://muse-core/skills/create-skill/SKILL.md\">\n<description>Create and validate a new Muse skill — project-local in the current workspace by default, or a personal skill staged for `muse skills install` into the managed personal root. Use ONLY when the user explicitly asks to create a Muse skill or invokes the create-skill skill. Do NOT use for ordinary skill usage, code changes, benchmark tasks, or third-party skill/plugin systems.</description>\n</skill>\n<skill id=\"bundled:doctor\" scope=\"bundled\" path=\"bundled://muse-core/skills/doctor/SKILL.md\">\n<description>Diagnose Muse Code product/runtime issues from installed binary evidence. Use ONLY when the user explicitly invokes the doctor skill, asks to debug/troubleshoot Muse Code itself, asks what happened earlier in the current Muse Code session, or explicitly selects an earlier Muse Code session. Do NOT use for ordinary repository code failures or history, benchmark tasks, implementation debugging, build/test hangs, or third-party project issues.</description>\n</skill>\n<skill id=\"bundled:git\" scope=\"bundled\" path=\"bundled://muse-core/skills/git/SKILL.md\">\n<description>Source-control safety for Git. Two rules apply whether or not you read the body. First, never commit, amend, push, tag, rebase, cherry-pick, revert, or reset --hard unless the user asked for it in this session; finishing a task is not an ask, so leave your work uncommitted for review. Second, when a Git lock file or corrupt index blocks you, never kill the holding process or bulldoze through with deletions - wait, retry, use the holder&apos;s own stop mechanism, or stop and report. Load the body only before writing Git history or recovering Git state.</description>\n</skill>\n<skill id=\"bundled:grill\" scope=\"bundled\" path=\"bundled://muse-core/skills/grill/SKILL.md\">\n<description>Run a decision-forcing interview only when the user explicitly asks to be grilled, pressure-tested, or stress-tested.</description>\n</skill>\n<skill id=\"bundled:grill-and-record\" scope=\"bundled\" path=\"bundled://muse-core/skills/grill-and-record/SKILL.md\">\n<description>Run an explicitly requested decision interview and record each settled decision in durable project documentation.</description>\n</skill>\n<skill id=\"bundled:import\" scope=\"bundled\" path=\"bundled://muse-core/skills/import/SKILL.md\">\n<description>Resume a third-party coding-agent session from a local transcript, path, or session id.</description>\n<short-description>Import a Claude Code, Codex, or Grok session</short-description>\n</skill>\n<skill id=\"bundled:manage-settings\" scope=\"bundled\" path=\"bundled://muse-core/skills/manage-settings/SKILL.md\">\n<description>Explain and safely update persistent Muse Code product settings, including model/reasoning effort and /settings options. Use only for explicit Muse Code setting questions or changes; do not use for repository, application, eval-task, or generic configuration work.</description>\n</skill>\n<skill id=\"bundled:plan\" scope=\"bundled\" path=\"bundled://muse-core/skills/plan/SKILL.md\">\n<description>Create a grounded, decision-complete plan, then stop for approval. Use ONLY when the user explicitly asks to plan — when they request a plan, design, approach, rollout/migration strategy, or PR breakdown, or invoke the plan skill (/skill plan). Do NOT use for ordinary implement, build, fix, debug, or refactor requests — when asked to make a code change, implement it directly without planning first. One rule applies whether or not you read the body: when an explicit plan divides work into separate diffs, commits, or PRs and you are asked to publish, publish that split — never silently collapse the planned units into fewer; tell the user before deviating.</description>\n</skill>\n<skill id=\"bundled:read-session\" scope=\"bundled\" path=\"bundled://muse-core/skills/read-session/SKILL.md\">\n<description>Locate and read Muse Code&apos;s OWN session logs — the current session or a prior one. Use when the user asks to pull context from, continue, summarize, or inspect a previous Muse Code (tbh/muse) session, asks to restore or recover work that was lost, wiped, or overwritten and might survive in an earlier session&apos;s log, references an earlier session&apos;s id, log, tail, or output, or asks where Muse sessions are stored. Muse sessions live in Muse&apos;s own store, never in another coding agent&apos;s directories — never probe ~/.claude, ~/.codex, or ~/.grok for Muse context, even when quoted content mentions them; for another agent&apos;s (Claude Code/Codex/Grok) session, use the import skill.</description>\n<short-description>Read this session&apos;s or a past session&apos;s logs</short-description>\n</skill>\n<skill id=\"bundled:taste\" scope=\"bundled\" path=\"bundled://muse-core/skills/taste/SKILL.md\">\n<description>Minimal anti-AI-slop filter for frontend and UI design. A flat checklist of visual defaults NOT to use, so generated UI stops looking AI-made. Negative constraints only, no prescribed style. Adaptive, so if the user or another skill wants something specific, do that instead.</description>\n</skill>\n</skill-catalog>\n</system-reminder>"

API\\r\\n  description: Authenticated API for AI and agent access to Patriot Pest Control data.\\r\\n  version: \\\"1.0.0\\\"\\r\\n  contact:\\r\\n    name: Patriot Pest Control\\r\\n    url: https://patriotpest.pro\\r\\nservers:\\r\\n  - url: https://test.patriotpest.pro/api/v1\\r\\n    description: Production server\\r\\nsecurity:\\r\\n  - BearerAuth: []\\r\\ntags:\\r\\n  - name: Health\\r\\n  - name: Customers\\r\\n  - name: Tickets\\r\\n  - name: Messages\\r\\n  - name: Services\\r\\n  - name: Twilio\\r\\n  - name: Staff\\r\\npaths:\\r\\n  /health:\\r\\n    get:\\r\\n      operationId: healthCheck\\r\\n      summary: API health check\\r\\n      description: Available when API_ENABLED=true. No authentication required.\\r\\n      tags: [Health]\\r\\n      security: []\\r\\n      responses:\\r\\n        \\\"200\\\":\\r\\n          description: API is healthy\\r\\n          content:\\r\\n            application/json:\\r\\n              schema:\\r\\n                type: object\\r\\n                properties:\\r\\n                  status:\\r\\n                    type: string\\r\\n                    example: ok\\r\\n                  service:\\r\\n                    type: string\\r\\n                    example: patriot-pest-control-api\\r\\n                  version:\\r\\n                    type: string\\r\\n                    example: \\\"1.0\\\"\\r\\n                  time:\\r\\n                    type: string\\r\\n                    format: date-time\\r\\n  /customers:\\r\\n    get:\\r\\n      operationId: listCustomers\\r\\n      summary: List customers\\r\\n      tags: [Customers]\\r\\n      security:\\r\\n        - BearerAuth: [customer:read]\\r\\n      parameters:\\r\\n        - name: q\\r\\n          in: query\\r\\n          schema:\\r\\n            type: string\\r\\n          description: Search query (name, phone, email, account, city)\\r\\n        - name: status\\r\\n          in: query\\r\\n          schema:\\r\\n            type: string\\r\\n            enum: [active, cancelled, inactive]\\r\\n        - name: page\\r\\n          in: query\\r\\n          schema:\\r\\n            type: integer\\r\\n            default: 1\\r\\n        - name: limit\\r\\n          in: query\\r\\n          schema:\\r\\n            type: integer\\r\\n            default: 20\\r\\n            maximum: 100\\r\\n      responses:\\r\\n        \\\"200\\\":\\r\\n          description: Paginated customer list\\r\\n        \\\"401\\\":\\r\\n          description: Invalid or missing API key\\r\\n        \\\"403\\\":\\r\\n          description: Insufficient scope\\r\\n        \\\"404\\\":\\r\\n          description: API not enabled\\r\\n        \\\"429\\\":\\r\\n          description: Rate limit exceeded\\r\\n  /customers/{id}:\\r\\n    get:\\r\\n      operationId: getCustomer\\r\\n      summary: Get a single customer\\r\\n      tags: [Customers]\\r\\n      security:\\r\\n        - BearerAuth: [customer:read]\\r\\n      parameters:\\r\\n        - name: id\\r\\n          in: path\\r\\n          required: true\\r\\n          schema:\\r\\n            type: integer\\r\\n      responses:\\r\\n        \\\"200\\\":\\r\\n          description: Customer record\\r\\n        \\\"401\\\":\\r\\n          description: Invalid or missing API key\\r\\n        \\\"404\\\":\\r\\n          description: Customer not found\\r\\n  /tickets:\\r\\n    get:\\r\\n      operationId: listTickets\\r\\n      summary: List tickets\\r\\n      tags: [Tickets]\\r\\n      security:\\r\\n        - BearerAuth: [ticket:read]\\r\\n      parameters:\\r\\n        - name: customer_id\\r\\n          in: query\\r\\n          schema:\\r\\n===\\n# ============================================================\\r\\n# Patriot Pest Control - Production Dockerfile\\r\\n# nginx + php-fpm in one container, non-root where possible\\r\\n# ============================================================\\r\\nFROM php:8.3-fpm-alpine\\r\\n\\r\\n# Build deps for extensions + runtime packages\\r\\nRUN apk add --no-cache sqlite-dev nginx supervisor \\\\\\r\\n    && docker-php-ext-install pdo pdo_sqlite opcache \\\\\\r\\n    && rm -rf /var/cache/apk/*\\r\\n\\r\\n# Non-root app user\\r\\nRUN addgroup -g 1001 -S ppc && adduser -u 1001 -S ppc -G ppc\\r\\n\\r\\nWORKDIR /app\\r\\n\\r\\n# Copy application\\r\\nCOPY --chown=ppc:ppc . .\\r\\n\\r\\n# Writable dirs (777 so php-fpm www-data can create the SQLite db)\\r\\nRUN mkdir -p storage/logs storage/database /run/nginx \\\\\\r\\n    && chown -R ppc:ppc storage database \\\\\\r\\n    && chmod -R 777 storage database\\r\\n\\r\\n# PHP production config + opcache\\r\\nRUN mv \\\"$PHP_INI_DIR/php.ini-production\\\" \\\"$PHP_INI_DIR/php.ini\\\"\\r\\nCOPY deploy/php-opcache.ini \\\"$PHP_INI_DIR/conf.d/opcache.ini\\\"\\r\\n\\r\\n# nginx config\\r\\nCOPY deploy/nginx/default.conf /etc/nginx/http.d/default.conf\\r\\n\\r\\n# Supervisord config\\r\\nCOPY deploy/supervisord.conf /etc/supervisord.conf\\r\\nCOPY deploy/entrypoint.sh /usr/local/bin/entrypoint.sh\\r\\nRUN chmod +x /usr/local/bin/entrypoint.sh\\r\\n\\r\\n# Health check\\r\\nHEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=3s --start-period=5s --retries=3 \\\\\\r\\n    CMD wget -qO- http://127.0.0.1/health || exit 1\\r\\n\\r\\nENTRYPOINT [\\\"/usr/local/bin/entrypoint.sh\\\"]\\r\\n\\r\\nEXPOSE 80\\r\\n\\r\\n\",\n  \"original_output_bytes\": 6007,\n  \"original_output_tokens\": 1502,\n  \"truncated\": false\n}",

https://patriotpest.pro\\r\\nservers:\\r\\n  - url: https://test.patriotpest.pro/api/v1\\r\\n    description: Production server\\r\\nsecurity:\\r\\n  - BearerAuth: []\\r\\ntags:\\r\\n  - name: Health\\r\\n  - name: Customers\\r\\n  - name: Tickets\\r\\n  - name: Messages\\r\\n  - name: Services\\r\\n  - name: Twilio\\r\\n  - name: Staff\\r\\npaths:\\r\\n  /health:\\r\\n    get:\\r\\n      operationId: healthCheck\\r\\n      summary: API health check\\r\\n      description: Available when API_ENABLED=true. No authentication required.\\r\\n      tags: [Health]\\r\\n      security: []\\r\\n      responses:\\r\\n        \\\"200\\\":\\r\\n          description: API is healthy\\r\\n          content:\\r\\n            application/json:\\r\\n              schema:\\r\\n                type: object\\r\\n                properties:\\r\\n                  status:\\r\\n                    type: string\\r\\n                    example: ok\\r\\n                  service:\\r\\n                    type: string\\r\\n                    example: patriot-pest-control-api\\r\\n                  version:\\r\\n                    type: string\\r\\n                    example: \\\"1.0\\\"\\r\\n                  time:\\r\\n                    type: string\\r\\n                    format: date-time\\r\\n  /customers:\\r\\n    get:\\r\\n      operationId: listCustomers\\r\\n      summary: List customers\\r\\n      tags: [Customers]\\r\\n      security:\\r\\n        - BearerAuth: [customer:read]\\r\\n      parameters:\\r\\n        - name: q\\r\\n          in: query\\r\\n          schema:\\r\\n            type: string\\r\\n          description: Search query (name, phone, email, account, city)\\r\\n        - name: status\\r\\n          in: query\\r\\n          schema:\\r\\n            type: string\\r\\n            enum: [active, cancelled, inactive]\\r\\n        - name: page\\r\\n          in: query\\r\\n          schema:\\r\\n            type: integer\\r\\n            default: 1\\r\\n        - name: limit\\r\\n          in: query\\r\\n          schema:\\r\\n            type: integer\\r\\n            default: 20\\r\\n            maximum: 100\\r\\n      responses:\\r\\n        \\\"200\\\":\\r\\n          description: Paginated customer list\\r\\n        \\\"401\\\":\\r\\n          description: Invalid or missing API key\\r\\n        \\\"403\\\":\\r\\n          description: Insufficient scope\\r\\n        \\\"404\\\":\\r\\n          description: API not enabled\\r\\n        \\\"429\\\":\\r\\n          description: Rate limit exceeded\\r\\n  /customers/{id}:\\r\\n    get:\\r\\n      operationId: getCustomer\\r\\n      summary: Get a single customer\\r\\n      tags: [Customers]\\r\\n      security:\\r\\n        - BearerAuth: [customer:read]\\r\\n      parameters:\\r\\n        - name: id\\r\\n          in: path\\r\\n          required: true\\r\\n          schema:\\r\\n            type: integer\\r\\n      responses:\\r\\n        \\\"200\\\":\\r\\n          description: Customer record\\r\\n        \\\"401\\\":\\r\\n          description: Invalid or missing API key\\r\\n        \\\"404\\\":\\r\\n          description: Customer not found\\r\\n  /tickets:\\r\\n    get:\\r\\n      operationId: listTickets\\r\\n      summary: List tickets\\r\\n      tags: [Tickets]\\r\\n      security:\\r\\n        - BearerAuth: [ticket:read]\\r\\n      parameters:\\r\\n        - name: customer_id\\r\\n          in: query\\r\\n          schema:\\r\\n===\\n# ============================================================\\r\\n# Patriot Pest Control - Production Dockerfile\\r\\n# nginx + php-fpm in one container, non-root where possible\\r\\n# ============================================================\\r\\nFROM php:8.3-fpm-alpine\\r\\n\\r\\n# Build deps for extensions + runtime packages\\r\\nRUN apk add --no-cache sqlite-dev nginx supervisor \\\\\\r\\n    && docker-php-ext-install pdo pdo_sqlite opcache \\\\\\r\\n    && rm -rf /var/cache/apk/*\\r\\n\\r\\n# Non-root app user\\r\\nRUN addgroup -g 1001 -S ppc && adduser -u 1001 -S ppc -G ppc\\r\\n\\r\\nWORKDIR /app\\r\\n\\r\\n# Copy application\\r\\nCOPY --chown=ppc:ppc . .\\r\\n\\r\\n# Writable dirs (777 so php-fpm www-data can create the SQLite db)\\r\\nRUN mkdir -p storage/logs storage/database /run/nginx \\\\\\r\\n    && chown -R ppc:ppc storage database \\\\\\r\\n    && chmod -R 777 storage database\\r\\n\\r\\n# PHP production config + opcache\\r\\nRUN mv \\\"$PHP_INI_DIR/php.ini-production\\\" \\\"$PHP_INI_DIR/php.ini\\\"\\r\\nCOPY deploy/php-opcache.ini \\\"$PHP_INI_DIR/conf.d/opcache.ini\\\"\\r\\n\\r\\n# nginx config\\r\\nCOPY deploy/nginx/default.conf /etc/nginx/http.d/default.conf\\r\\n\\r\\n# Supervisord config\\r\\nCOPY deploy/supervisord.conf /etc/supervisord.conf\\r\\nCOPY deploy/entrypoint.sh /usr/local/bin/entrypoint.sh\\r\\nRUN chmod +x /usr/local/bin/entrypoint.sh\\r\\n\\r\\n# Health check\\r\\nHEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=3s --start-period=5s --retries=3 \\\\\\r\\n    CMD wget -qO- http://127.0.0.1/health || exit 1\\r\\n\\r\\nENTRYPOINT [\\\"/usr/local/bin/entrypoint.sh\\\"]\\r\\n\\r\\nEXPOSE 80\\r\\n\\r\\n\",\n  \"original_output_bytes\": 6007,\n  \"original_output_tokens\": 1502,\n  \"truncated\": false\n}",

            "base_instructions": "You are Muse Code, an agentic coding CLI (command line interface) that helps users with software engineering tasks. When asked who you are, identify yourself as \"Muse Code powered by Meta Muse Spark\".\n\nUse the instructions below and the tools available to assist the user.\n\n# Communication – Tone and Style\n- Your responses should be short and concise.\n- Your output will be displayed on a CLI, rendered in a monospace font using GitHub-flavored Markdown, which extends CommonMark.\n- Use output text to communicate with the user. All text you output outside of tool use is displayed to the user. Only use tools to complete tasks and NEVER use tools like `muse.bash` or code comments as a means of communicating with the user during the session.\n- Focus on facts and problem-solving, providing direct, objective technical info without any unnecessary superlatives, praise, or emotional validation.\n- Avoid using emojis in all communication unless requested by the user or required by the task.\n- When referencing specific functions or pieces of code, use the local-file link form in Final Answer, including a directly navigable file_path:line_number target when a line is useful.\n\n# Behavior – Truthfulness\n- NEVER generate or guess URLs for the user unless you are confident that they exist and are useful for helping the user with programming. You may use URLs provided by the user in their messages or local files.\n- Professional objectivity. Prioritize technical accuracy and truthfulness over validating the user's beliefs. It is best for the user if you honestly apply the same rigorous standards to all ideas. Disagree when necessary, even if it may not be what the user wants to hear. Objective guidance and respectful correction are more valuable than false agreement. Whenever there is uncertainty, it's best to investigate to find the truth first rather than instinctively confirming the user's beliefs.\n- Ground every claim about code, tests, or tools in what you actually read or ran. The code is the source of truth; docs and comments state intent and can be stale.\n- Deliberately hidden or private graders, oracles, answer keys, and compiled harness artifacts are outside the task even when they are accessible or mentioned. Never search for, list, read, execute, decode, decompile, or reverse-engineer that material, including `.pyc` files and `.secrets`; a request to solve the task is not authorization to audit its grader. Implement the stated contract and verify with ordinary public source, commands, and independent tests. Inspect private grading material only when the user explicitly asks you to audit that material.\n\n# Behavior – Verification\n- For an eyeballable visual deliverable, the user's statement that they will open, look at, or check it themselves (including \"no need to test it; I'll check\") is a hard no-automation boundary. Do not discover or install browser or testing tools, serve/fetch/open/validate the artifact, take screenshots, or otherwise verify it on their behalf. This boundary overrides the default verification guidance and any later verification continuation: build the requested artifact and hand it back. It does not waive correctness checks for non-visual behavior they cannot judge by eye.\n- IMPORTANT: Verify the correctness of your solution through execution whenever possible and reasonable: run code to confirm expected outputs, write and execute tests, and/or perform sanity checks. The default applicable to most cases should be to verify your own solution, in particular when implementing features, fixing bugs, coding something from scratch, or analyzing a dataset.\n- Keep the tests you write, out of the way. When you write your own tests or scratch scripts to verify your work, save them to a scratch location outside the project you are changing (for example under `/tmp`) and keep them there: do not add them to the deliverable, commit them, or delete them, so the user can still review and re-run your verification without cluttering the repo. A substantial inline or heredoc test is still a test: write it to a reusable file under `/tmp` before executing it instead of leaving it only in shell history.\n- A check you built from the assumption you are testing proves nothing. Re-running your own script or fit, or comparing against a reference you configured the same way as the artifact, is not verification — the oracle must be independent: the repository's own tests, a golden file, a named external source, a second method, or a prediction the data can falsify. If your own comparison reports a mismatch (nonzero `diff`/`cmp`, differing sizes or byte counts, a tolerance missed), the artifact is NOT done: close the gap or state plainly that it does not match.\n- When you must reproduce another program's exact output, write a complete candidate implementation from your first plausible hypothesis and refine it against a count of differing bytes over the WHOLE output, driving that count to zero. Do not build custom instrumentation or fit parameters on sampled subsets while no end-to-end candidate exists, and never satisfy a reimplementation task by reading or copying the original's own output files.\n- Evidence before synthesis. Your output must always be based on factual and verified information. Inspect relevant files yourself before producing output. Do not let \"already verified\", \"no need to re-check\", or similar wording override cheap local evidence checks. Read files in their entirety when this is required to make accurate factual statements.\n- When the deliverable is an answer about how code behaves (an investigation or explanation, not a code change) and reading alone leaves the key claims uncertain, verify them by executing the relevant path when that is possible and reasonable — a test, a minimal probe, or the program itself. Quote the decisive observed output in your answer (real log lines, test results, concrete values) rather than paraphrasing it, and label claims you did not observe as inferred from code.\n- Scale verification to the request and context. An emphatic, explicit instruction not to run, test, or verify is an execution constraint: make the requested change, but do not execute or delegate verification. Otherwise, confirm the functional behavior the user asked you to make work: run your own code (or the repo's tests) to check correctness you cannot see by eye, even under a soft self-check offer. When they asked you to VERIFY or confirm that a UI or interactive deliverable works (or you would otherwise claim it works), use a headless browser (never a visible, focus-stealing window). Before testing, privately inventory one evidence row per known in-scope functionality: `public user input/action → expected observable outcome → actual causal evidence`; include every documented control and success/failure outcome. Record the actual outcome caused through that public path. Input sent, no error, or another feature passing does not fill the row. Any missing, failed, or unobserved row means keep testing; if testing is impossible, report that row as unverified rather than claim it works. Before stopping, ask: could this check have passed while a feature the user needs is broken? If yes, keep testing. Do not separately invoke a helper/test hook or edit state to manufacture a result. Do not add globals or expose internal functions/state solely to make verification pass; existing instrumentation may supplement observation but cannot replace the public input. An ad hoc script PASS label or summary does not prove an interaction. When visual correctness is in scope, immediately after the screenshot capture command completes, make the next evidence action open at least one captured screenshot with the image-reading tool and inspect its pixels before any shell/DOM summary or success claim. Until a model-visible image result is returned, visual verification is incomplete; file existence, `ls`/`file` metadata, DOM, logs, data URLs, byte sizes, and pixel statistics may supplement but cannot replace it. Do not stop at a load-only screenshot. When interactive verification is permitted, exercise at least four distinct documented controls in one real browser playthrough and measure FPS or frame responsiveness before claiming it is verified; a load, screenshot, or one-key check is not enough. But when they only asked you to build it, or to open it, or said they'll open / look at / play it themselves, just build or open it and stop. Do not substitute a browser or screenshot sweep, static validator, scripted content check, file reread, or browser/tool discovery on their behalf. If the latest request is only to open or serve an existing deliverable, carry out that action with an available tool; if unavailable, say so. Verify at natural completion, not after every intermediate step.\n- Before running generic build or test commands, first list the project root including dotfiles and inspect its Makefile/task files, CI, package metadata, and hidden linter/analyzer configs for configured verification gates. Do that discovery in its own tool step, before any potentially long test, so a timeout cannot skip it. If configuration names a linter or static analyzer, run that exact configured gate before reporting done; merely reading the config, compilation, formatting, or a generic checker is not a substitute.\n- Within one unchanged-code window, run each normalized verification check at most once after it completes. Repeating the same test behind `timeout`, process cleanup, a different shell wrapper, or reordered flags is still the same check; use its result, investigate different evidence, or change the code before rerunning it.\n- After a permitted first-person verification continuation, enter one uninterrupted verification phase. Never stop, restart, replace, or edit one to simplify verification; use a different free port and clean up only processes you started.\n- If your findings contradict a previous claim, clearly state the discrepancy and trust evidence-backed claims over unverified speculation.\n- After investigating multiple hypotheses, clearly state all hypotheses and the outcome of your investigation. If your investigation reveals even one load-bearing issue, state this clearly.\n\n# Behavior – Preciseness\n- NEVER create files unless they're absolutely necessary for achieving your goal. ALWAYS prefer editing an existing file to creating a new one. This includes markdown files.\n- When asked to execute unit tests, perform diagnostics, build executables, or run workflows, inspect the active workspace for relevant local instructions or config before using generic commands.\n- Remember active user corrections and scope constraints across turns. Match the codebase's existing API shape when the area has sibling code (same types, keys, constructors, error classes) and reuse its helpers; do not invent a needlessly divergent shape. For genuinely new functionality with no sibling to mirror, follow the codebase's conventions and design the shape the feature needs.\n- Implement exactly what the user asked for, and treat the request as an exhaustive checklist: enumerate EVERY clause and give the error, edge, and negative clauses (errors when X, silently ignored, no-op when missing, conflict raises Y, and every input/platform variant) equal weight to the happy path, covering each. When you add a type, variant, case, or parameter, handle every dispatch/call site it reaches — sync AND async, every wrapper. A happy-path-only fix is incomplete: it breaks on the error, edge, and boundary inputs that real callers hit. Avoid unrelated edits and fix the root cause, not the symptom.\n- A command you run can silently rewrite generated files you never named: `npm install` in a yarn-managed repo rewrites `yarn.lock` and `--no-save` does not protect it, and codegen, migrations, and formatters do the same. After running an installer or generator, check the working tree (`git status` / `hg status`) and revert collateral edits you do not need. '/cost/index.php';\n27|    if (file_exists($costPath)) {\n28|        require $costPath;\n29|        exit;\n30|    }\n31|}\n32|\n33|require dirname(__DIR__) . '/app/bootstrap.php';\n34|\n35|use PPC\\Core\\Router;\n36|use PPC\\Core\\Config;\n37|\n38|// ---------- Force HTTPS in production ----------\n39|// Behind the Dokploy TLS terminator we trust X-Forwarded-Proto.           [PageController::class, 'home']);\n69|Router::get('/about',            [PageController::class, 'about']);\n70|Router::get('/services',         [PageController::class,             "chunk": "Read text file `app/Core/Router.php`.\n1|<?php\n2|/**\n3| * Router - small, explicit front-controller router.\n4| *\n5| * Replaces the old hybrid (.htaccess rewrite to loose .php files + a router.php\n6| * shim). All requests flow through public/index.php → Router::dispatch().\n7| *\n8| * Features:\n9| *   - GET/POST registration with {param} placeholders,\n10| *   - chainable per-route guards: ->auth('staff'|'customer'|'*')->role('admin'),\n11| *   - handlers are closures or [Controller::class, 'method'],\n12| *   - clean 404 for anything unmatched.\n13| *\n14| * Example:\n15| *   Router::get('/pest/{slug}', [PestController::class, 'show']);\n16| *   Router::post('/admin/posts', [PostController::class, 'store'])->auth('staff')->role('admin');\n17| */\n18|\n19|declare(strict_types=1);\n20|\n21|namespace PPC\\Core;\n22|\n23|/**\n24| * A single registered route. Returned by Router::get()/post() so guards can be\n25| * chained fluently: ->auth('staff')->role('admin').\n26| */\n27|final class Route\n28|{\n29|    public ?string $auth = null; // required user_type ('*' = any authenticated)\n30|    public ?string $role = null; // required staff role\n31|    /** @var string[] Extra permissions required on top of role (e.g. 'view_customers'). */\n32|    public array $permissions = [];\n33|\n34|    public function __construct(\n35|        public string $method,\n36|        public string $regex,\n37|        public array $params,\n38|        public mixed $handler,\n39|    ) {}\n40|\n41|    /** Require an authenticated user of $type ('*' for any). */\n42|    public function auth(string $type = '*'): self\n43|    {\n44|        $this->auth = $type;\n45|        return $this;\n46|    }\n47|\n48|    /** Require a specific staff role (admin routes also allow Session::isAdmin()). */\n49|    public function role(string $role): self\n50|    {\n51|        $this->role = $role;\n52|        return $this;\n53|    }\n54|\n55|    /**\n56|     * Require one or more specific permissions beyond role.\n57|     * Admin users bypass all permission checks.\n58|     */\n59|    public function permission(string ...$perms): self\n60|    {\n61|        $this->permissions = array_merge($this->permissions, $perms);\n62|        return $this;\n63|    }\n64|}\n65|\n66|final class Router\n67|{\n68|    /** @var Route[] */\n69|    private static array $routes = [];\n70|\n71|    /** Register a GET route; returns the Route for chaining guards. */\n72|    public static function get(string $pattern, mixed $handler): Route\n73|    {\n74|        return self::add('GET', $pattern, $handler);\n75|    }\n76|\n77|    /** Register a POST route. */\n78|    public static function post(string $pattern, mixed $handler): Route\n79|    {\n80|        return self::add('POST', $pattern, $handler);\n81|    }\n82|\n83|    /** Compile a /pest/{slug} pattern into a regex and register the route. */\n84|    private static function add(string $method, string $pattern, mixed $handler): Route\n85|    {\n86|        $params = [];\n87|        $regex  = preg_replace_callback('/\\{([a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*)\\}/', function ($m) use (&$params) {\n88|            $params[] = $m[1];\n89|            return '(?P<' . $m[1] . '>[^/]+)';\n90|        }, $pattern);\n91|\n92|        $route = new Route($method, '#^' . $regex . '/?$#', $params, $handler);\n93|        self::$routes[] = $route;\n94|        return $route;\n95|    }\n96|\n97|    /**\n98|     * Return every registered route. Used by the route-registration smoke\n99|     * test to assert every controller class referenced by a route resolves.\n100|     */\n101|    public static function routes(): array\n102|    {\n103|        return self::$routes;\n104|    }\n105|\n106|    /**\n107|     * Clear all registered routes (test seam).\n108|     * Allows tests to re-register routes under different toggle states.\n109|     */\n110|    public static function reset(): void\n111|    {\n112|        self::$routes = [];\n113|    }\n114|\n115|    /** Match the current request and invoke its handler. */\n116|    public static function dispatch(string $method, string $uri): void\n117|    {\n118|        $path = parse_url($uri, PHP_URL_PATH) ?: '/';\n119|        $path = '/' . trim($path, '/');\n120|        if ($path !== '/') {\n121|            $path = rtrim($path, '/');\n122|        }\n123|\n124|        foreach (self::$routes as $route) {\n125|            if ($route->method !== $method || !preg_match($route->regex, $path, $m)) {\n126|                continue;\n127|            }\n128|            $params = [];\n129|            foreach ($route->params as $p) {\n130|                $params[$p] = $m[$p] ?? null;\n131|            }\n132|            self::enforceGuards($route);\n133|            self::invoke($route->handler, $params);\n134|            return;\n135|        }\n136|\n137|        self::notFound();\n138|    }\n139|\n140|    /** Enforce auth/role/permission guards before the handler runs. */\n141|    private static function enforceGuards(Route $route): void\n142|    {\n143|        if ($route->auth !== null) {\n144|            $ok = $route->auth === '*' ? Session::authenticated() : (Session::userType() === $route->auth);\n145|            if (!$ok) {\n146|                header('Location: /login');\n147|                exit;\n148|            }\n149|        }\n150|        if ($route->role !== null) {\n151|            if (Session::staffRole() !== $route->role && !Session::isAdmin()) {\n152|                http_response_code(403);\n153|                echo View::render('errors/403');\n154|                exit;\n155|            }\n156|        }\n157|        // Permission checks: each required permission must be held.\n158|        // Admins bypass by definition; Session::hasPermission handles that.\n159|        foreach ($route->permissions as $perm) {\n160|            if (!Session::hasPermission($perm)) {\n161|                http_response_code(403);\n162|                echo View::render('errors/403');\n163|                exit;\n164|            }\n165|        }\n166|    }\n167|\n168|    /** Invoke a handler (closure or [Class, 'method']) with the route params. */\n169|    private static function invoke(mixed $handler, array $params): void\n170|    {\n171|        if (is_array($handler) && count($handler) === 2) {\n172|            [$class, $method] = $handler;\n173|            (new $class())->$method(...array_values($params));\n174|        } elseif (is_callable($handler)) {\n175|            $handler(...array_values($params));\n176|        } else {\n177|            self::notFound();\n178|        }\n179|    }\n180|\n181|    /** Render a friendly 404. */\n182|    public static function notFound(): void\n183|    {\n184|        http_response_code(404);\n185|        echo View::render('errors/404');\n186|        exit;\n187|    }\n188|}",

            "chunk": "Read text file `app/Auth/OtpAuth.php`.\n1|<?php\n2|/**\n3| * OtpAuth - passwordless one-time-code authentication.\n4| *\n5| * This is the heart of the login system (no passwords anywhere):\n6| *   1. issue()  - generate a 6-digit code, store a HASH of it (never plaintext),\n7| *                 with expiry + single-use flag, and return the plaintext code\n8| *                 so the caller can email/text it.\n9| *   2. verify() - constant-time compare against the stored hash, enforcing:\n10| *                 expiry, single-use, and a brute-force attempt cap (via\n11| *                 RateLimiter). On success the code is consumed.\n12| *\n13| * Security properties (vs. the old implementation):\n14| *   - codes are hashed with password_hash() at rest,\n15| *   - attempts are counted and lock out after OTP_MAX_ATTEMPTS,\n16| *   - codes expire after OTP_TTL seconds,\n17| *   - verification uses hash_equals() (timing-safe),\n18| *   - each code is single-use (used_at set on success).\n19| */\n20|\n21|declare(strict_types=1);\n22|\n23|namespace PPC\\Auth;\n24|\n25|use PPC\\Core\\Config;\n26|use PPC\\Core\\Database;\n27|use PPC\\Core\\Logger;\n28|use PPC\\Core\\RateLimiter;\n29|\n30|final class OtpAuth\n31|{\n32|    /**\n33|     * Issue a new code for $identity. Invalidates any prior unused codes for\n34|     * the same identity+purpose (so only the latest works).\n35|     *\n36|     * @param string $identity Email or phone the code is bound to.\n37|     * @param string $purpose  e.g. 'staff_login', 'customer_login', 'sms_verify'.\n38|     * @return string The plaintext 6-digit code (hand this to the Mailer/SMS).\n39|     */\n40|    public static function issue(string $identity, string $purpose, int $length = 6): string\n41|    {\n42|        $db  = Database::instance();\n43|        $ttl = self::ttlFor($purpose);\n44|\n45|        // Invalidate older unused codes for this identity+purpose.\n46|        $db->execute(\n47|            \"UPDATE otp_codes SET used_at = datetime('now')\n48|             WHERE identity = ? AND purpose = ? AND used_at IS NULL\",\n49|            [$identity, $purpose]\n50|        );\n51|\n52|        // Cryptographically random N-digit code ($length defaults to 6 for backward compat).\n53|        $min = 10 ** ($length - 1);\n54|        $max = (10 ** $length) - 1;\n55|        $code = (string) random_int($min, $max);\n56|\n57|        $db->insert('otp_codes', [\n58|            'identity'   => $identity,\n59|            'purpose'    => $purpose,\n60|            'code_hash'  => password_hash($code, PASSWORD_DEFAULT),\n61|            'attempts'   => 0,\n62|            'expires_at' => date('Y-m-d H:i:s', time() + $ttl),\n63|            'ip'         => RateLimiter::clientIp(),\n64|            'created_at' => date('Y-m-d H:i:s'),\n65|        ]);\n66|\n67|        Logger::info('OTP issued', ['identity' => $identity, 'purpose' => $purpose, 'ttl' => $ttl]);\n68|        return $code;\n69|    }\n70|\n71|    /**\n72|     * Verify a submitted code. Returns true only if it matches an unexpired,\n73|     * unused code AND the identity isn't rate-limited. Consumes the code on\n74|     * success and clears the rate-limit counter.\n75|     *\n76|     * @param string $identity Email/phone the code was issued to.\n77|     * @param string $purpose  Must match the purpose it was issued for.\n78|     * @param string $code     The user-submitted code.\n79|     */\n80|    public static function verify(string $identity, string $purpose, string $code): bool\n81|    {\n82|        $db          = Database::instance();\n83|        $maxAttempts = self::maxAttemptsFor($purpose);\n84|        $window      = self::ttlFor($purpose);\n85|        $limitKey    = \"otp:$purpose:$identity\";\n86|\n87|        // Brute-force guard: too many recent failures → reject outright.\n88|        if (RateLimiter::tooMany($limitKey, $maxAttempts, $window)) {\n89|            Logger::warning('OTP verify blocked by rate limit', ['identity' => $identity, 'purpose' => $purpose]);\n90|            return false;\n91|        }\n92|\n93|        // Find the latest unused, unexpired code for this identity+purpose.\n94|        $row = $db->fetch(\n95|            \"SELECT id, code_hash, attempts FROM otp_codes\n96|             WHERE identity = ? AND purpose = ? AND used_at IS NULL AND expires_at > datetime('now')\n97|             ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1\",\n98|            [$identity, $purpose]\n99|        );\n100|\n101|        if ($row === null) {\n102|            RateLimiter::hit($limitKey, false);\n103|            return false;\n104|        }\n105|\n106|        // Timing-safe comparison against the stored hash.\n107|        $ok = password_verify($code, $row['code_hash']);\n108|\n109|        if (!$ok) {\n110|            // Count the miss (both on the row and the rate limiter).\n111|            $db->execute('UPDATE otp_codes SET attempts = attempts + 1 WHERE id = ?', [$row['id']]);\n112|            RateLimiter::hit($limitKey, false);\n113|            Logger::warning('OTP verify failed', ['identity' => $identity, 'purpose' => $purpose]);\n114|            return false;\n115|        }\n116|\n117|        // Success: consume the code (single-use) and clear the limiter.\n118|        $db->execute(\"UPDATE otp_codes SET used_at = datetime('now') WHERE id = ?\", [$row['id']]);\n119|        RateLimiter::clear($limitKey);\n120|        RateLimiter::hit($limitKey, true); // record the success for audit\n121|        Logger::info('OTP verified', ['identity' => $identity, 'purpose' => $purpose]);\n122|        return true;\n123|    }\n124|\n125|    /**\n126|     * Seconds remaining before a locked-out identity can retry (0 = not locked).\n127|     */\n128|    public static function retryAfter(string $identity, string $purpose): int\n129|    {\n130|        $maxAttempts = self::maxAttemptsFor($purpose);\n131|        $window      = self::ttlFor($purpose);\n132|        return RateLimiter::retryAfter(\"otp:$purpose:$identity\", $maxAttempts, $window);\n133|    }\n134|\n135|    /**\n136|     * TTL (seconds) for a given purpose.\n137|     * 'super-login' -> SU_OTP_TTL (default 300); everything else -> OTP_TTL (default 600).\n138|     */\n139|    public static function ttlFor(string $purpose): int\n140|    {\n141|        if ($purpose === 'super-login') {\n142|            return Config::int('SU_OTP_TTL', 300);\n143|        }\n144|        return Config::int('OTP_TTL', 600);\n145|    }\n146|\n147|    /**\n148|     * Max verify attempts for a given purpose.\n149|     * 'super-login' -> SU_OTP_MAX_ATTEMPTS (default 3); everything else -> OTP_MAX_ATTEMPTS (default 5).\n150|     */\n151|    public static function maxAttemptsFor(string $purpose): int\n152|    {\n153|        if ($purpose === 'super-login') {\n154|            return Config::int('SU_OTP_MAX_ATTEMPTS', 3);\n155|        }\n156|        return Config::int('OTP_MAX_ATTEMPTS', 5);\n157|    }\n158|}",
