            "chunk": "Read text file `PLANS/MASTERPLAN_PASSWORDLESS_EMAIL_CODE.md`.\n1|# Masterplan: Superuser + Passwordless Email-Code Login\n2|\n3|## Context (what exists)\n4|\n5|The app already has **passwordless email-OTP login for everyone** (`AuthController`, `OtpAuth`, `Mailer`). There are no passwords anywhere. When a user enters an identifier (email/phone/account), the system matches staff first (by email), then customers, issues a 6-digit code hashed with `password_hash()`, emails it, verifies it with `hash_equals()`, and opens a role-routed session. The existing admin role has `[\"all\"]` permissions and gates every admin route via `->auth(\"staff\")->role(\"admin\")`.\n6|\n7|This masterplan is **not** building passwordless login from scratch. It is adding a **dedicated, elevated superuser surface** that is toggleable, isolated from the standard login flow, and carries stronger security guarantees.\n8|\n9|## What DavidPatton asked for\n10|\n11|1. `david@itak.net` becomes a superuser -- a tier above admin\n12|2. When logging in, no password -- enter email, get an emailed code, enter the code, get in\n13|3. \"Secure 2nd auth\" -- the emailed code IS the second factor (possession of the inbox)\n14|\n15|## Architecture\n16|\n17|### Standard login isolation (BLOCKER 1 FIX -- Cybersecurity review)\n18|\n19|The superuser account MUST NOT be reachable through the standard `/login` flow. The dedicated `/su` surface is the sole path. Two defenses:\n20|\n21|**Defense 1: loginRequest() exclusion.** Add `AND role != 'super-user'` to the staff lookup in `AuthController::loginRequest()`:\n22|\n23|```php\n24|$staff = $db->fetch(\n25|    \"SELECT id, email, name, role FROM staff WHERE email = ? AND active = 1 AND role != 'super-user'\",\n26|    [$email]\n27|);\n28|```\n29|\n30|Without this filter, the seeded super-user row matches the standard staff lookup, the system issues a 6-digit code (600s TTL, 5 attempts), and `startStaffSession()` sets `staff_role='super-user'`, routing to `/admin`. The super-user is reachable under the materially weaker standard controls -- 6 vs 8 digits (~91x fewer guesses), 5 vs 3 attempts, 2x the window -- and the `/su` hardening is bypassable even when the toggle is OFF.\n31|\n32|**Defense 2: startStaffSession() guard (defense in depth).** At the top of `startStaffSession()`, fail closed if the resolved row has role `'super-user'`:\n33|\n34|```php\n35|if (($row['role'] ?? '') === 'super-user') {\n36|    throw new \\RuntimeException('Super-user must authenticate via /su surface only.');\n37|}\n38|```\n39|\n40|This ensures that even if a future code change accidentally removes the SQL filter, the session is never established for a super-user through the standard path. The exception is logged and the user sees a generic error.\n41|\n42|**Phpunit:** `test_superuser_blocked_from_standard_login` -- loginRequest() with super-user email returns null (no code issued). `test_superuser_session_guard_denies_superuser` -- startStaffSession() with role='super-user' throws RuntimeException.\n43|\n44|### Layer separation\n45|\n46|```\n47|/su              Superuser login surface (toggleable -- separate from /login)\n48|/admin/*         Admin CMS (unchanged, existing admin guards)\n49|/login           Standard unified login (unchanged, existing)\n50|```\n51|\n52|The superuser surface is a **parallel auth path**, not a modification to the existing `/login`. If `SUPERUSER_ENABLED=false`, `/su` and `/su/verify` return 404 and zero superuser routes register. The standard login is never affected.\n53|\n54|### Flow\n55|\n56|1. User navigates to `/su` -- a dedicated superuser login page (single email field, no identifier matching)\n57|2. User enters email -- POST `/su`\n58|3. Email validated with `filter_var($email, FILTER_VALIDATE_EMAIL)` -- reject CR/LF and non-email input before any DB lookup\n59|4. System looks up the email in the `staff` table where `role = 'super-user'` AND `active = 1`\n60|5. If match: issues a code, emails it, redirects to `/su/verify` (code entry)\n61|6. On `/su/verify`: user enters code -- POST `/su/verify`\n62|7. Code verified -- session established with `staff_role = 'super-user'`\n63|8. Redirected to `/admin` (the CMS)\n64|\n65|Mismatch behavior: if the email does not belong to a super-user, the system shows the same \"code sent\" screen (enumeration defense), but no code is issued. Verification will fail, and the user sees \"code incorrect.\"\n66|\n67|### Why a separate surface\n68|\n69|| Property | Standard `/login` | Superuser `/su` |\n70||---|---|---|\n71|| Identifier matching | Matches staff by email, then customers by email/phone/account | Matches ONLY super-user staff by email |\n72|| Email validation | Loose (trim, max:120) | Strict (FILTER_VALIDATE_EMAIL, CR/LF rejected) |\n73|| Enumeration defense | Shows \"code sent\" for no-match (same defense) | Same |\n74|| Rate limit (request) | 5/min per IP + 3/5min per identity | 3/min per IP + 2/5min per identity (tighter) |\n75|| OTP length | 6 digits | 8 digits |\n76|| OTP TTL | OTP_TTL (default 600s) | SU_OTP_TTL (default 300s, shorter) |\n77|| Max verify attempts | OTP_MAX_ATTEMPTS (default 5) | 3 (tighter, hardcoded) |\n78|| Session idle | SESSION_LIFETIME_STAFF (7200s) | 3600s (shorter for superuser) |\n79|| Feature toggle | None (always on) | SUPERUSER_ENABLED (default false) |\n80|| Dev mail log gate | Config::isLocal() only | Same -- staging host has APP_ENV != local so codes never written to disk |\n81|\n82|## Database changes\n83|\n84|### New role: super-user\n85|\n86|```sql\n87|INSERT OR IGNORE INTO roles (role, label, permissions) VALUES\n88|    ('super-user', 'Super User', '[\"all\"]');\n89|```\n90|\n91|The `\"all\"` permission already exists on the admin role and grants bypass in `Session::hasPermission()`. The super-user role carries the same permission set (`\"all\"`) but is an **immutable role** -- the staff CRUD cannot change a super-user's role field or deactivate them.\n92|\n93|### Seed migration (idempotent, run at startup by Database.php)\n94|\n95|The seed reads `SU_SEED_EMAIL` from config. If the staff row exists with a different role, it is promoted to `'super-user'` via UPDATE. If it does not exist, it is INSERTed with name 'David Patton' and role `'super-user'`. The grant is audit-logged:\n96|\n97|```php\n98|$db->insert('audit_log', [\n99|    'user_id'   => null,           // system\n100|    'user_type' => 'system',\n101|    'action'    => 'superuser.grant',\n102|    'entity'    => 'staff',\n103|    'entity_id' => (string) $staffId,\n104|    'meta_json' => json_encode(['email' => $email, 'role' => 'super-user']),\n105|    'ip'        => RateLimiter::clientIp(),\n106|    'created_at' => date('Y-m-d H:i:s'),\n107|]);\n108|```\n109|\n110|The grant is fully idempotent across three scenarios:\n111|\n112|1. **Empty `SU_SEED_EMAIL`:** If `Config::get('SU_SEED_EMAIL')` returns null or empty string, the seed migration exits immediately with zero queries. No staff row is created, no audit log written. This is the default behavior when `.env` omits the variable -- superuser surface can be toggled on later by setting the env var and restarting.\n113|2. **Already-promoted super-user:** If the staff row already has `role = 'super-user'`, the migration is a no-op -- no UPDATE, no audit row. The check `SELECT role FROM staff WHERE email = ?` returns `'super-user'` and the migration skips.\n114|3. **New promotion:** If the staff row exists with a non-superuser role, it is UPDATEd to `'super-user'` and exactly one `audit_log` row is inserted with `action = 'superuser.grant'`. Re-running the migration after this hits scenario 2 (no-op).\n115|\n116|Implementation sketch:\n117|\n118|```php\n119|$email = Config::get('SU_SEED_EMAIL');\n120|if (!$email || trim($email) === '') {\n121|    return; // No-op on empty config\n122|}\n123|\n124|$existing = $db->fetch(\"SELECT id, role FROM staff WHERE email = ?\", [$email]);\n125|if (!$existing) {\n126|    // INSERT new row\n127|    $db->insert('staff', [...]);\n128|    $this->auditGrant($staffId, $email);\n129|} elseif ($existing['role'] !== 'super-user') {\n130|    // UPDATE existing to super-user\n131|    $db->execute(\"UPDATE staff SET role = 'super-user' WHERE id = ?\", [$existing['id']]);\n132|    $this->auditGrant($existing['id'], $email);\n133|}\n134|// else: already super-user, no-op\n135|```\n136|\n137|### New env vars in .env.example\n138|\n139|```\n140|# --- Superuser login (dedicated elevated surface) ---\n141|# Toggleable: when false, /su and /su/verify return 404.\n142|SUPERUSER_ENABLED=false\n143|# OTP validity for superuser codes (seconds, shorter than staff default).\n144|SU_OTP_TTL=300\n145|# Seed email -- the account promoted to super-user on first migration.\n146|SU_SEED_EMAIL=david@itak.net\n147|```\n148|\n149|## Route registration (public/index.php)\n150|\n151|```php\n152|// ---------- Superuser login (toggleable, elevated surface) ----------\n153|if (\\PPC\\Core\\Config::bool(\"SUPERUSER_ENABLED\", false)) {\n154|    Router::get(\"/su\",             [AuthController::class, \"superLoginForm\"]);\n155|    Router::post(\"/su\",            [AuthController::class, \"superLoginRequest\"]);\n156|    Router::get(\"/su/verify\",      [AuthController::class, \"superLoginVerifyForm\"]);\n157|    Router::post(\"/su/verify\",     [AuthController::class, \"superLoginVerify\"]);\n158|}\n159|```\n160|\n161|Four routes, four new controller methods, one new template (`templates/auth/super-login.php`). The verify form reuses `templates/auth/verify.php` with `purpose = 'super-login'`.\n162|\n163|## Controller changes (AuthController.php)\n164|\n165|Four new methods:\n166|\n167|### `superLoginForm()` -- GET /su\n168|- If already authenticated as super-user, redirect to /admin\n169|- Renders `auth/super-login` (email-only form)\n170|\n171|### `superLoginRequest()` -- POST /su\n172|- CSRF verify\n173|- Validate email with `filter_var($email, FILTER_VALIDATE_EMAIL)`, reject CR/LF, max 254 chars\n174|- Rate limit: 3/min per IP via `RateLimiter::clientIp()` (XFF-aware, tighter than standard)\n175|- Look up staff where email = ? AND role = 'super-user' AND active = 1\n176|- On match: `issueAndEmailSuper($email)` -- 8-digit code, `SU_OTP_TTL`, purpose `'super-login'`\n177|- Stash `pending_login_email`, `pending_login_type = 'staff'`, `pending_login_id` in session\n178|- Flash \"code sent\"\n179|- On mismatch: same flash, no code issued (enumeration defense)\n180|- Redirect to `/su/verify`\n181|\n182|### `superLoginVerify()` -- POST /su/verify\n183|- CSRF verify\n184|- Read pending_login state from session\n185|- `OtpAuth::verify($email, 'super-login', $code)` -- purpose isolation\n186|- On success: `startSuperSession($email)` -- same pattern as `startStaffSession()` but:\n187|  - Role check: enforces `role = 'super-user'` (fail closed)\n188|  - Session regenerate (fixation defense)\n189|  - Session put: `staff_role = 'super-user'`\n190|  - Audit log: `action = 'super-login'`, `ip` via `RateLimiter::clientIp()`\n191|  - Redirect to `/admin`\n192|- On failure: same error handling as existing flow\n193|\n194|### Helper: `issueAndEmailSuper(string $email)`\n195|- Rate limit: 2 codes per identity per 5 minutes (tighter)\n196|- `OtpAuth::issue($email, 'super-login', 8)` -- 8-digit code\n197|- TTL from `Config::int('SU_OTP_TTL', 300)`\n198|- `Mailer::send()` with branded template\n199|- Dev mail log gated by `Config::isLocal()` (existing behavior, no change)\n200|\n201|## OtpAuth changes\n202|\n203|Add optional `$length` parameter (default 6 for backward compat):\n204|\n205|```php\n206|public static function issue(string $identity, string $purpose, int $length = 6): string\n207|{\n208|    $min = 10 ** ($length - 1);\n209|    $max = (10 ** $length) - 1;\n210|    $code = (string) random_int($min, $max);\n211|    // ... hash + insert as before\n212|}\n213|```\n214|\n215|Superuser calls pass `$length = 8`. All existing calls default to 6 (zero behavior change). `verify()` is unchanged.\n216|\n217|**IP attribution fix (Cybersecurity Note 1):** `OtpAuth::issue()` currently records `$_SERVER['REMOTE_ADDR']` (the proxy IP behind Dokploy). For accurate attribution, change the `ip` column insert to use `RateLimiter::clientIp()` (XFF-aware):\n218|\n219|```php\n220|// In OtpAuth::issue(), change:\n221|'ip' => RateLimiter::clientIp(),\n222|```\n223|\n224|This is a one-line fix with zero behavioral change beyond IP accuracy. Enforcement already uses `clientIp()` via `RateLimiter`. Applies to all OTP purposes, not just super-login, fixing the proxy-blind spot globally.\n225|\n226|## Session changes\n227|\n228|```php\n229|public static function isSuperUser(): bool\n230|{\n231|    return self::staffRole() === 'super-user';\n232|}\n233|\n234|public static function isAdmin(): bool\n235|{\n236|    return self::staffRole() === 'admin' || self::staffRole() === 'super-user';\n237|}\n238|```\n239|\n240|This makes **all** admin-guarded routes available to super-users with zero route changes. One fix needed in `AuthController::dashboardFor()`:\n241|\n242|```php\n243|return ($role === 'admin' || $role === 'super-user') ? '/admin' : '/staff-dashboard';\n244|```\n245|\n246|### enforceIdleTimeout() superuser specialization (Cybersecurity Note 2)\n247|\n248|The existing `Session::enforceIdleTimeout()` gives all staff the same 7200s idle timeout. Special-case super-user for a stricter 3600s idle window:\n249|\n250|```php\n251|public static function enforceIdleTimeout(): void\n252|{\n253|    if (!self::isStaff()) return;\n254|\n255|    $lifetime = (self::staffRole() === 'super-user') ? 3600 : self::SESSION_LIFETIME_STAFF;\n256|    $lastActivity = $_SESSION['last_activity'] ?? 0;\n257|\n258|    if (time() - $lastActivity > $lifetime) {\n259|        self::logout();\n260|        header('Location: /login?timeout=1');\n261|        exit;\n262|    }\n263|    $_SESSION['last_activity'] = time();\n264|}\n265|```\n266|\n267|Superuser sessions expire after 3600s idle (half the standard 7200s). The `last_activity` key is bumped on every authenticated request via router middleware, same as today.\n268|\n269|## Immutability protections\n270|\n271|The staff CRUD must refuse to modify a super-user:\n272|\n273|**staffUpdate() guard:**\n274|```php\n275|$target = $db->fetch('SELECT role FROM staff WHERE id = ?', [$id]);\n276|if ($target['role'] === 'super-user') {\n277|    Session::flash('staff', ['error' => 'Super-user accounts cannot be modified.']);\n278|    header('Location: /admin/staff');\n279|    exit;\n280|}\n281|```\n282|\n283|**staffToggle() guard:**\n284|```php\n285|$target = $db->fetch('SELECT role FROM staff WHERE id = ?', [$id]);\n286|if ($target['role'] === 'super-user') {\n287|    Session::flash('staff', ['error' => 'Super-user accounts cannot be deactivated.']);\n288|    header('Location: /admin/staff');\n289|    exit;\n290|}\n291|```\n292|\n293|## Mapping to Cybersecurity Security Bar\n294|\n295|| Bar | Requirement | Implementation |\n296||---|---|---|\n297|| 1 | Code entropy | 8-digit CSPRNG via `random_int(10**7, 10**8-1)`, ~23 bits |\n298|| 2 | Code at rest | `password_hash()` via existing `OtpAuth::issue()` |\n299|| 3 | Constant-time verify | `password_verify()` + `hash_equals()` via existing `OtpAuth::verify()` |\n300|| 4 | Single-use | `used_at` consumed on success; new issue invalidates prior unused codes |\n301|| 5 | Expiry | `SU_OTP_TTL` 300s default, hard expiry in verify SQL |\n302|| 6 | Rate limit (issue) | 2 codes per identity per 5 min + 3 per IP per min |\n303|| 7 | Rate limit (verify) | 3 attempts per identity per TTL window |\n304|| 8 | Session fixation | `Session::regenerate()` on login (existing, reused) |\n305|| 9 | Session idle timeout | 3600s for superuser (vs 7200s staff) |\n306|| 10 | Enumeration defense | Same \"code sent\" flash for no-match; no timing difference |\n307|| 11 | Superuser immutability | Staff CRUD cannot change role or deactivate |\n308|| 12 | No secrets in repo | `SU_SEED_EMAIL` from .env (git-ignored) |\n309|| 13 | Feature toggle | `SUPERUSER_ENABLED=false` -- routes never register, 404 |\n310|| 14 | CSRF | All POST routes: `Csrf::verifyOrDie()` |\n311|| 15 | Email header injection | `filter_var(FILTER_VALIDATE_EMAIL)` + CR/LF rejection before any send; Mailer uses fixed headers |\n312|| 16 | Auth audit trail | `audit_log` rows for `superuser.grant`, `super-login`, `logout` with `RateLimiter::clientIp()` |\n313|| 17 | Purpose isolation | `'super-login'` purpose; standard `'login'` codes cannot cross-authenticate |\n314|| 18 | Dev mail log gate | `Config::isLocal()` only (existing); staging APP_ENV != local |\n315|| 19 | Grant audit trail | `audit_log` row for seed grant with `user_type='system'`, `action='superuser.grant'` |\n316|| 20 | Role equivalence | `isAdmin()` returns true for super-user; all guard chains, `hasPermission()`, and `dashboardFor()` handle it |\n317|\n318|## Phpunit coverage\n319|\n320|| Test | What it asserts |\n321||---|---|\n322|| `test_superuser_role_seeded` | roles table has 'super-user' with [\"all\"] |\n323|| `test_superuser_email_seeded` | staff row exists for SU_SEED_EMAIL |\n324|| `test_superuser_grant_audit_logged` | audit_log row for superuser.grant |\n325|| `test_superuser_code_entropy` | 8-digit, within [10000000, 99999999] |\n326|| `test_superuser_code_single_use` | code consumed, second verify fails |\n327|| `test_superuser_code_expiry` | expired code rejected |\n328|| `test_superuser_purpose_isolation` | 'login' code fails 'super-login' verify |\n329|| `test_superuser_rate_limit_verify` | 3 attempts locks out |\n330|| `test_superuser_immutable_role` | Staff CRUD update rejected |\n331|| `test_superuser_immutable_deactivate` | Staff CRUD toggle rejected |\n332|| `test_superuser_disabled_toggle_404` | SUPERUSER_ENABLED=false, /su not registered |\n333|| `test_superuser_isAdmin_gate` | Session::isAdmin() true for super-user |\n334|| `test_superuser_dashboard_routing` | dashboardFor() routes to /admin |\n335|| `test_superuser_blocked_from_standard_login` | loginRequest() excludes super-user email (null, no code issued) |\n336|| `test_superuser_session_guard_denies_superuser` | startStaffSession() with role='super-user' throws RuntimeException |\n337|\n338|Route-registration smoke test (existing) covers superuser routes when SUPERUSER_ENABLED=true.\n339|\n340|## Toggle lifecycle\n341|\n342|- `SUPERUSER_ENABLED=false` (default): zero superuser routes register. `/su` returns standard 404. Seed migration still runs at startup (role promoted, account created, audit-logged), but the super-user account is blocked from standard `/login` by Defense 1 (`AND role != 'super-user'` filter in `loginRequest()`) and Defense 2 (`startStaffSession()` guard). The dedicated `/su` path does not exist. The account exists but no auth path reaches it.\n343|- `SUPERUSER_ENABLED=true`: four routes register, `/su` login surface is live. Super-user authenticates through the dedicated elevated surface with 8-digit codes, 300s TTL, and 3 max attempts. Standard `/login` continues to exclude the super-user (Defense 1 still active).\n344|- No other feature depends on this toggle. Safe to enable/disable at any time.\n345|\n346|## What this does NOT touch\n347|\n348|- **Standard `/login` flow for non-superuser staff and customers:** unchanged, zero impact. The single change (`AND role != 'super-user'` in `loginRequest()`) is a one-line exclusion that only prevents super-user accounts from authenticating through the weaker path; all other identities are unaffected.\n349|- Zero changes to `otp_codes` schema\n350|- Zero changes to `Mailer` or `RateLimiter` (used as-is, except `OtpAuth` IP attribution fix which improves accuracy globally)\n351|- Zero customer-record reads or writes\n352|- Zero changes to admin CMS route guards (superuser inherits access via `isAdmin()`)\n353|- Zero hardcoded emails or secrets in any committed file",

                "text": "Read text file `PLANS/MASTERPLAN_PASSWORDLESS_EMAIL_CODE.md`.\n1|# Masterplan: Superuser + Passwordless Email-Code Login\n2|\n3|## Context (what exists)\n4|\n5|The app already has **passwordless email-OTP login for everyone** (`AuthController`, `OtpAuth`, `Mailer`). There are no passwords anywhere. When a user enters an identifier (email/phone/account), the system matches staff first (by email), then customers, issues a 6-digit code hashed with `password_hash()`, emails it, verifies it with `hash_equals()`, and opens a role-routed session. The existing admin role has `[\"all\"]` permissions and gates every admin route via `->auth(\"staff\")->role(\"admin\")`.\n6|\n7|This masterplan is **not** building passwordless login from scratch. It is adding a **dedicated, elevated superuser surface** that is toggleable, isolated from the standard login flow, and carries stronger security guarantees.\n8|\n9|## What DavidPatton asked for\n10|\n11|1. `david@itak.net` becomes a superuser -- a tier above admin\n12|2. When logging in, no password -- enter email, get an emailed code, enter the code, get in\n13|3. \"Secure 2nd auth\" -- the emailed code IS the second factor (possession of the inbox)\n14|\n15|## Architecture\n16|\n17|### Standard login isolation (BLOCKER 1 FIX -- Cybersecurity review)\n18|\n19|The superuser account MUST NOT be reachable through the standard `/login` flow. The dedicated `/su` surface is the sole path. Two defenses:\n20|\n21|**Defense 1: loginRequest() exclusion.** Add `AND role != 'super-user'` to the staff lookup in `AuthController::loginRequest()`:\n22|\n23|```php\n24|$staff = $db->fetch(\n25|    \"SELECT id, email, name, role FROM staff WHERE email = ? AND active = 1 AND role != 'super-user'\",\n26|    [$email]\n27|);\n28|```\n29|\n30|Without this filter, the seeded super-user row matches the standard staff lookup, the system issues a 6-digit code (600s TTL, 5 attempts), and `startStaffSession()` sets `staff_role='super-user'`, routing to `/admin`. The super-user is reachable under the materially weaker standard controls -- 6 vs 8 digits (~91x fewer guesses), 5 vs 3 attempts, 2x the window -- and the `/su` hardening is bypassable even when the toggle is OFF.\n31|\n32|**Defense 2: startStaffSession() guard (defense in depth).** At the top of `startStaffSession()`, fail closed if the resolved row has role `'super-user'`:\n33|\n34|```php\n35|if (($row['role'] ?? '') === 'super-user') {\n36|    throw new \\RuntimeException('Super-user must authenticate via /su surface only.');\n37|}\n38|```\n39|\n40|This ensures that even if a future code change accidentally removes the SQL filter, the session is never established for a super-user through the standard path. The exception is logged and the user sees a generic error.\n41|\n42|**Phpunit:** `test_superuser_blocked_from_standard_login` -- loginRequest() with super-user email returns null (no code issued). `test_superuser_session_guard_denies_superuser` -- startStaffSession() with role='super-user' throws RuntimeException.\n43|\n44|### Layer separation\n45|\n46|```\n47|/su              Superuser login surface (toggleable -- separate from /login)\n48|/admin/*         Admin CMS (unchanged, existing admin guards)\n49|/login           Standard unified login (unchanged, existing)\n50|```\n51|\n52|The superuser surface is a **parallel auth path**, not a modification to the existing `/login`. If `SUPERUSER_ENABLED=false`, `/su` and `/su/verify` return 404 and zero superuser routes register. The standard login is never affected.\n53|\n54|### Flow\n55|\n56|1. User navigates to `/su` -- a dedicated superuser login page (single email field, no identifier matching)\n57|2. User enters email -- POST `/su`\n58|3. Email validated with `filter_var($email, FILTER_VALIDATE_EMAIL)` -- reject CR/LF and non-email input before any DB lookup\n59|4. System looks up the email in the `staff` table where `role = 'super-user'` AND `active = 1`\n60|5. If match: issues a code, emails it, redirects to `/su/verify` (code entry)\n61|6. On `/su/verify`: user enters code -- POST `/su/verify`\n62|7. Code verified -- session established with `staff_role = 'super-user'`\n63|8. Redirected to `/admin` (the CMS)\n64|\n65|Mismatch behavior: if the email does not belong to a super-user, the system shows the same \"code sent\" screen (enumeration defense), but no code is issued. Verification will fail, and the user sees \"code incorrect.\"\n66|\n67|### Why a separate surface\n68|\n69|| Property | Standard `/login` | Superuser `/su` |\n70||---|---|---|\n71|| Identifier matching | Matches staff by email, then customers by email/phone/account | Matches ONLY super-user staff by email |\n72|| Email validation | Loose (trim, max:120) | Strict (FILTER_VALIDATE_EMAIL, CR/LF rejected) |\n73|| Enumeration defense | Shows \"code sent\" for no-match (same defense) | Same |\n74|| Rate limit (request) | 5/min per IP + 3/5min per identity | 3/min per IP + 2/5min per identity (tighter) |\n75|| OTP length | 6 digits | 8 digits |\n76|| OTP TTL | OTP_TTL (default 600s) | SU_OTP_TTL (default 300s, shorter) |\n77|| Max verify attempts | OTP_MAX_ATTEMPTS (default 5) | 3 (tighter, hardcoded) |\n78|| Session idle | SESSION_LIFETIME_STAFF (7200s) | 3600s (shorter for superuser) |\n79|| Feature toggle | None (always on) | SUPERUSER_ENABLED (default false) |\n80|| Dev mail log gate | Config::isLocal() only | Same -- staging host has APP_ENV != local so codes never written to disk |\n81|\n82|## Database changes\n83|\n84|### New role: super-user\n85|\n86|```sql\n87|INSERT OR IGNORE INTO roles (role, label, permissions) VALUES\n88|    ('super-user', 'Super User', '[\"all\"]');\n89|```\n90|\n91|The `\"all\"` permission already exists on the admin role and grants bypass in `Session::hasPermission()`. The super-user role carries the same permission set (`\"all\"`) but is an **immutable role** -- the staff CRUD cannot change a super-user's role field or deactivate them.\n92|\n93|### Seed migration (idempotent, run at startup by Database.php)\n94|\n95|The seed reads `SU_SEED_EMAIL` from config. If the staff row exists with a different role, it is promoted to `'super-user'` via UPDATE. If it does not exist, it is INSERTed with name 'David Patton' and role `'super-user'`. The grant is audit-logged:\n96|\n97|```php\n98|$db->insert('audit_log', [\n99|    'user_id'   => null,           // system\n100|    'user_type' => 'system',\n101|    'action'    => 'superuser.grant',\n102|    'entity'    => 'staff',\n103|    'entity_id' => (string) $staffId,\n104|    'meta_json' => json_encode(['email' => $email, 'role' => 'super-user']),\n105|    'ip'        => RateLimiter::clientIp(),\n106|    'created_at' => date('Y-m-d H:i:s'),\n107|]);\n108|```\n109|\n110|The grant is fully idempotent across three scenarios:\n111|\n112|1. **Empty `SU_SEED_EMAIL`:** If `Config::get('SU_SEED_EMAIL')` returns null or empty string, the seed migration exits immediately with zero queries. No staff row is created, no audit log written. This is the default behavior when `.env` omits the variable -- superuser surface can be toggled on later by setting the env var and restarting.\n113|2. **Already-promoted super-user:** If the staff row already has `role = 'super-user'`, the migration is a no-op -- no UPDATE, no audit row. The check `SELECT role FROM staff WHERE email = ?` returns `'super-user'` and the migration skips.\n114|3. **New promotion:** If the staff row exists with a non-superuser role, it is UPDATEd to `'super-user'` and exactly one `audit_log` row is inserted with `action = 'superuser.grant'`. Re-running the migration after this hits scenario 2 (no-op).\n115|\n116|Implementation sketch:\n117|\n118|```php\n119|$email = Config::get('SU_SEED_EMAIL');\n120|if (!$email || trim($email) === '') {\n121|    return; // No-op on empty config\n122|}\n123|\n124|$existing = $db->fetch(\"SELECT id, role FROM staff WHERE email = ?\", [$email]);\n125|if (!$existing) {\n126|    // INSERT new row\n127|    $db->insert('staff', [...]);\n128|    $this->auditGrant($staffId, $email);\n129|} elseif ($existing['role'] !== 'super-user') {\n130|    // UPDATE existing to super-user\n131|    $db->execute(\"UPDATE staff SET role = 'super-user' WHERE id = ?\", [$existing['id']]);\n132|    $this->auditGrant($existing['id'], $email);\n133|}\n134|// else: already super-user, no-op\n135|```\n136|\n137|### New env vars in .env.example\n138|\n139|```\n140|# --- Superuser login (dedicated elevated surface) ---\n141|# Toggleable: when false, /su and /su/verify return 404.\n142|SUPERUSER_ENABLED=false\n143|# OTP validity for superuser codes (seconds, shorter than staff default).\n144|SU_OTP_TTL=300\n145|# Seed email -- the account promoted to super-user on first migration.\n146|SU_SEED_EMAIL=david@itak.net\n147|```\n148|\n149|## Route registration (public/index.php)\n150|\n151|```php\n152|// ---------- Superuser login (toggleable, elevated surface) ----------\n153|if (\\PPC\\Core\\Config::bool(\"SUPERUSER_ENABLED\", false)) {\n154|    Router::get(\"/su\",             [AuthController::class, \"superLoginForm\"]);\n155|    Router::post(\"/su\",            [AuthController::class, \"superLoginRequest\"]);\n156|    Router::get(\"/su/verify\",      [AuthController::class, \"superLoginVerifyForm\"]);\n157|    Router::post(\"/su/verify\",     [AuthController::class, \"superLoginVerify\"]);\n158|}\n159|```\n160|\n161|Four routes, four new controller methods, one new template (`templates/auth/super-login.php`). The verify form reuses `templates/auth/verify.php` with `purpose = 'super-login'`.\n162|\n163|## Controller changes (AuthController.php)\n164|\n165|Four new methods:\n166|\n167|### `superLoginForm()` -- GET /su\n168|- If already authenticated as super-user, redirect to /admin\n169|- Renders `auth/super-login` (email-only form)\n170|\n171|### `superLoginRequest()` -- POST /su\n172|- CSRF verify\n173|- Validate email with `filter_var($email, FILTER_VALIDATE_EMAIL)`, reject CR/LF, max 254 chars\n174|- Rate limit: 3/min per IP via `RateLimiter::clientIp()` (XFF-aware, tighter than standard)\n175|- Look up staff where email = ? AND role = 'super-user' AND active = 1\n176|- On match: `issueAndEmailSuper($email)` -- 8-digit code, `SU_OTP_TTL`, purpose `'super-login'`\n177|- Stash `pending_login_email`, `pending_login_type = 'staff'`, `pending_login_id` in session\n178|- Flash \"code sent\"\n179|- On mismatch: same flash, no code issued (enumeration defense)\n180|- Redirect to `/su/verify`\n181|\n182|### `superLoginVerify()` -- POST /su/verify\n183|- CSRF verify\n184|- Read pending_login state from session\n185|- `OtpAuth::verify($email, 'super-login', $code)` -- purpose isolation\n186|- On success: `startSuperSession($email)` -- same pattern as `startStaffSession()` but:\n187|  - Role check: enforces `role = 'super-user'` (fail closed)\n188|  - Session regenerate (fixation defense)\n189|  - Session put: `staff_role = 'super-user'`\n190|  - Audit log: `action = 'super-login'`, `ip` via `RateLimiter::clientIp()`\n191|  - Redirect to `/admin`\n192|- On failure: same error handling as existing flow\n193|\n194|### Helper: `issueAndEmailSuper(string $email)`\n195|- Rate limit: 2 codes per identity per 5 minutes (tighter)\n196|- `OtpAuth::issue($email, 'super-login', 8)` -- 8-digit code\n197|- TTL from `Config::int('SU_OTP_TTL', 300)`\n198|- `Mailer::send()` with branded template\n199|- Dev mail log gated by `Config::isLocal()` (existing behavior, no change)\n200|\n201|## OtpAuth changes\n202|\n203|Add optional `$length` parameter (default 6 for backward compat):\n204|\n205|```php\n206|public static function issue(string $identity, string $purpose, int $length = 6): string\n207|{\n208|    $min = 10 ** ($length - 1);\n209|    $max = (10 ** $length) - 1;\n210|    $code = (string) random_int($min, $max);\n211|    // ... hash + insert as before\n212|}\n213|```\n214|\n215|Superuser calls pass `$length = 8`. All existing calls default to 6 (zero behavior change). `verify()` is unchanged.\n216|\n217|**IP attribution fix (Cybersecurity Note 1):** `OtpAuth::issue()` currently records `$_SERVER['REMOTE_ADDR']` (the proxy IP behind Dokploy). For accurate attribution, change the `ip` column insert to use `RateLimiter::clientIp()` (XFF-aware):\n218|\n219|```php\n220|// In OtpAuth::issue(), change:\n221|'ip' => RateLimiter::clientIp(),\n222|```\n223|\n224|This is a one-line fix with zero behavioral change beyond IP accuracy. Enforcement already uses `clientIp()` via `RateLimiter`. Applies to all OTP purposes, not just super-login, fixing the proxy-blind spot globally.\n225|\n226|## Session changes\n227|\n228|```php\n229|public static function isSuperUser(): bool\n230|{\n231|    return self::staffRole() === 'super-user';\n232|}\n233|\n234|public static function isAdmin(): bool\n235|{\n236|    return self::staffRole() === 'admin' || self::staffRole() === 'super-user';\n237|}\n238|```\n239|\n240|This makes **all** admin-guarded routes available to super-users with zero route changes. One fix needed in `AuthController::dashboardFor()`:\n241|\n242|```php\n243|return ($role === 'admin' || $role === 'super-user') ? '/admin' : '/staff-dashboard';\n244|```\n245|\n246|### enforceIdleTimeout() superuser specialization (Cybersecurity Note 2)\n247|\n248|The existing `Session::enforceIdleTimeout()` gives all staff the same 7200s idle timeout. Special-case super-user for a stricter 3600s idle window:\n249|\n250|```php\n251|public static function enforceIdleTimeout(): void\n252|{\n253|    if (!self::isStaff()) return;\n254|\n255|    $lifetime = (self::staffRole() === 'super-user') ? 3600 : self::SESSION_LIFETIME_STAFF;\n256|    $lastActivity = $_SESSION['last_activity'] ?? 0;\n257|\n258|    if (time() - $lastActivity > $lifetime) {\n259|        self::logout();\n260|        header('Location: /login?timeout=1');\n261|        exit;\n262|    }\n263|    $_SESSION['last_activity'] = time();\n264|}\n265|```\n266|\n267|Superuser sessions expire after 3600s idle (half the standard 7200s). The `last_activity` key is bumped on every authenticated request via router middleware, same as today.\n268|\n269|## Immutability protections\n270|\n271|The staff CRUD must refuse to modify a super-user:\n272|\n273|**staffUpdate() guard:**\n274|```php\n275|$target = $db->fetch('SELECT role FROM staff WHERE id = ?', [$id]);\n276|if ($target['role'] === 'super-user') {\n277|    Session::flash('staff', ['error' => 'Super-user accounts cannot be modified.']);\n278|    header('Location: /admin/staff');\n279|    exit;\n280|}\n281|```\n282|\n283|**staffToggle() guard:**\n284|```php\n285|$target = $db->fetch('SELECT role FROM staff WHERE id = ?', [$id]);\n286|if ($target['role'] === 'super-user') {\n287|    Session::flash('staff', ['error' => 'Super-user accounts cannot be deactivated.']);\n288|    header('Location: /admin/staff');\n289|    exit;\n290|}\n291|```\n292|\n293|## Mapping to Cybersecurity Security Bar\n294|\n295|| Bar | Requirement | Implementation |\n296||---|---|---|\n297|| 1 | Code entropy | 8-digit CSPRNG via `random_int(10**7, 10**8-1)`, ~23 bits |\n298|| 2 | Code at rest | `password_hash()` via existing `OtpAuth::issue()` |\n299|| 3 | Constant-time verify | `password_verify()` + `hash_equals()` via existing `OtpAuth::verify()` |\n300|| 4 | Single-use | `used_at` consumed on success; new issue invalidates prior unused codes |\n301|| 5 | Expiry | `SU_OTP_TTL` 300s default, hard expiry in verify SQL |\n302|| 6 | Rate limit (issue) | 2 codes per identity per 5 min + 3 per IP per min |\n303|| 7 | Rate limit (verify) | 3 attempts per identity per TTL window |\n304|| 8 | Session fixation | `Session::regenerate()` on login (existing, reused) |\n305|| 9 | Session idle timeout | 3600s for superuser (vs 7200s staff) |\n306|| 10 | Enumeration defense | Same \"code sent\" flash for no-match; no timing difference |\n307|| 11 | Superuser immutability | Staff CRUD cannot change role or deactivate |\n308|| 12 | No secrets in repo | `SU_SEED_EMAIL` from .env (git-ignored) |\n309|| 13 | Feature toggle | `SUPERUSER_ENABLED=false` -- routes never register, 404 |\n310|| 14 | CSRF | All POST routes: `Csrf::verifyOrDie()` |\n311|| 15 | Email header injection | `filter_var(FILTER_VALIDATE_EMAIL)` + CR/LF rejection before any send; Mailer uses fixed headers |\n312|| 16 | Auth audit trail | `audit_log` rows for `superuser.grant`, `super-login`, `logout` with `RateLimiter::clientIp()` |\n313|| 17 | Purpose isolation | `'super-login'` purpose; standard `'login'` codes cannot cross-authenticate |\n314|| 18 | Dev mail log gate | `Config::isLocal()` only (existing); staging APP_ENV != local |\n315|| 19 | Grant audit trail | `audit_log` row for seed grant with `user_type='system'`, `action='superuser.grant'` |\n316|| 20 | Role equivalence | `isAdmin()` returns true for super-user; all guard chains, `hasPermission()`, and `dashboardFor()` handle it |\n317|\n318|## Phpunit coverage\n319|\n320|| Test | What it asserts |\n321||---|---|\n322|| `test_superuser_role_seeded` | roles table has 'super-user' with [\"all\"] |\n323|| `test_superuser_email_seeded` | staff row exists for SU_SEED_EMAIL |\n324|| `test_superuser_grant_audit_logged` | audit_log row for superuser.grant |\n325|| `test_superuser_code_entropy` | 8-digit, within [10000000, 99999999] |\n326|| `test_superuser_code_single_use` | code consumed, second verify fails |\n327|| `test_superuser_code_expiry` | expired code rejected |\n328|| `test_superuser_purpose_isolation` | 'login' code fails 'super-login' verify |\n329|| `test_superuser_rate_limit_verify` | 3 attempts locks out |\n330|| `test_superuser_immutable_role` | Staff CRUD update rejected |\n331|| `test_superuser_immutable_deactivate` | Staff CRUD toggle rejected |\n332|| `test_superuser_disabled_toggle_404` | SUPERUSER_ENABLED=false, /su not registered |\n333|| `test_superuser_isAdmin_gate` | Session::isAdmin() true for super-user |\n334|| `test_superuser_dashboard_routing` | dashboardFor() routes to /admin |\n335|| `test_superuser_blocked_from_standard_login` | loginRequest() excludes super-user email (null, no code issued) |\n336|| `test_superuser_session_guard_denies_superuser` | startStaffSession() with role='super-user' throws RuntimeException |\n337|\n338|Route-registration smoke test (existing) covers superuser routes when SUPERUSER_ENABLED=true.\n339|\n340|## Toggle lifecycle\n341|\n342|- `SUPERUSER_ENABLED=false` (default): zero superuser routes register. `/su` returns standard 404. Seed migration still runs at startup (role promoted, account created, audit-logged), but the super-user account is blocked from standard `/login` by Defense 1 (`AND role != 'super-user'` filter in `loginRequest()`) and Defense 2 (`startStaffSession()` guard). The dedicated `/su` path does not exist. The account exists but no auth path reaches it.\n343|- `SUPERUSER_ENABLED=true`: four routes register, `/su` login surface is live. Super-user authenticates through the dedicated elevated surface with 8-digit codes, 300s TTL, and 3 max attempts. Standard `/login` continues to exclude the super-user (Defense 1 still active).\n344|- No other feature depends on this toggle. Safe to enable/disable at any time.\n345|\n346|## What this does NOT touch\n347|\n348|- **Standard `/login` flow for non-superuser staff and customers:** unchanged, zero impact.         "durability": "durable",
        "id": "fc1ba6aa-834b-49da-bfd6-b186138d6ce5",
        "payload": {
          "event": {
            "chunk": "{\n  \"chunk_id\": \"exec-12-1\",\n  \"command\": \"cat /mnt/g/Mojo/patriot-pest-app/public/assets/app.css 2>&1 | head -n 200; echo \\\"===\\\"; cat /mnt/g/Mojo/patriot-pest-app/public/assets/styles.css 2>&1 | head -n 200; echo \\\"===\\\"; cat /mnt/g/Mojo/patriot-pest-app/templates/layouts/main.php 2>&1 | head -n 150; echo \\\"===\\\"; cat /mnt/g/Mojo/patriot-pest-app/public/assets/app.js 2>&1 | head -n 150\",\n  \"description\": \"Inspect patriotic theme and crosshair\",\n  \"exit_code\": 0,\n  \"terminal_status\": \"completed\",\n  \"output\": \"/* ==========================================================================\\r\\n   app.css - the LIGHT authenticated app shell.\\r\\n\\r\\n   The marketing site is dark (olive/cream). The authenticated areas - staff\\r\\n   dashboard, customer portal, and the CMS - flip to a clean, paper-white\\r\\n   workspace so staff can read data all day without fatigue.\\r\\n\\r\\n   How it works: every component in admin.css/styles.css is driven by the CSS\\r\\n   custom properties defined in styles.css :root. We RE-DECLARE those vars on\\r\\n   body.appshell-body, mapping the dark olive ramp onto a light paper ramp.\\r\\n   Everything downstream (panels, tables, badges, forms, buttons) re-skins\\r\\n   automatically - no per-component overrides needed except where a component\\r\\n   hard-codes a dark color (notices, table headers) which we fix below.\\r\\n\\r\\n   Layout: a fixed LEFT sidebar (desktop) that collapses to an off-canvas\\r\\n   drawer + a sticky 5-icon bottom bar (mobile). The center bottom icon is a\\r\\n   raised magnifier that opens the customer search overlay (staff/admin).\\r\\n   ========================================================================== */\\r\\n\\r\\n/* ---------- 1. light palette: remap the dark vars onto paper ---------- */\\r\\nbody.appshell-body {\\r\\n  background: #f4f2ea;\\r\\n  color: #23281c;\\r\\n\\r\\n  /* dark olive ramp  ->  light paper ramp */\\r\\n  --olive-950: #ffffff;   /* deepest surface (form inputs) -> white        */\\r\\n  --olive-900: #fbfaf5;   /* recessed surface (table wrap)  -> near-white  */\\r\\n  --olive-800: #ffffff;   /* raised cards / panels          -> white       */\\r\\n  --olive-700: #e4e0d2;   /* hairline borders               -> warm gray    */\\r\\n  --olive-500: #cfc9b6;   /* stronger borders / focus ring  -> stone        */\\r\\n  --olive-300: #6d7c46;   /* olive accent text (readable on white)         */\\r\\n  --khaki:     #7b7460;   /* muted labels / secondary text                 */\\r\\n  --cream:     #23281c;   /* PRIMARY text -> dark ink                      */\\r\\n  --paper:     #ece4cd;\\r\\n  --paper-dark:#ddd0ac;\\r\\n  /* --orange / --orange-hot / --red / --ink keep their values: they read\\r\\n     well as accents on white. Link orange is darkened below for contrast. */\\r\\n\\r\\n  /* shell-specific tokens */\\r\\n  --shell-bg:      #f4f2ea;\\r\\n  --shell-side:    #ffffff;\\r\\n  --shell-line:    #e4e0d2;\\r\\n  --shell-ink:     #23281c;\\r\\n  --shell-muted:   #7b7460;\\r\\n  --shell-accent:  #f4772e;\\r\\n  --shell-accent-d:#c8551a;   /* darker orange for text links (AA on white) */\\r\\n  --shell-hover:   #f6f1e6;\\r\\n  --shell-shadow:  0 1px 2px rgba(35,40,28,.06), 0 8px 24px rgba(35,40,28,.06);\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\n/* readable text links (keep buttons/CTAs their own colors) */\\r\\nbody.appshell-body :where(a):not(.btn):not(.nav-cta):not(.appshell-brand):not(.appshell-nav a):not(.appshell-bar a):not(.appshell-user) {\\r\\n  color: var(--shell-accent-d);\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\n/* ---------- 2. fix components that hard-coded dark colors ---------- */\\r\\n/* notices: the dark-theme text colors (cream / #ffd9d2) would vanish on white */\\r\\nbody.appshell-body .notice          { color: var(--shell-ink); }\\r\\nbody.appshell-body .notice.success  { background: #eef3e2; border-color: #b9c98f; color: #33401f; }\\r\\nbody.appshell-body .notice.error    { background: #fbeae6; border-color: #e0a89c; color: #8a2c1c; }\\r\\nbody.appshell-body .notice.info     { background: #fdeee1; border-color: #f0c19c; color: #8a4a1c; }\\r\\n\\r\\n/* table header lost its dark fill (olive-800 -> white); give it a soft tint */\\r\\nbody.appshell-body table.data th        { background: #f0ede2; color: #6b6450; }\\r\\nbody.appshell-body table.data tr:hover td { background: rgba(244,119,46,.06); }\\r\\nbody.appshell-body .table-wrap          { border-color: var(--shell-line); background: #fff; }\\r\\n\\r\\n/* cards get a soft shadow + border instead of the dark border-only look */\\r\\nbody.appshell-body .panel,\\r\\nbody.appshell-body .stat-card,\\r\\nbody.appshell-body .tile,\\r\\nbody.appshell-body .media-item { box-shadow: var(--shell-shadow); }\\r\\nbody.appshell-body .tile:hover { border-color: var(--shell-accent); box-shadow: 0 10px 28px rgba(244,119,46,.14); }\\r\\n\\r\\n/* ghost button: dark text + stone ring on white */\\r\\nbody.appshell-body .btn-ghost { color: var(--shell-ink); box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 2px var(--olive-500); }\\r\\nbody.appshell-body .btn-ghost:hover { color: var(--shell-accent-d); box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 2px var(--shell-accent); }\\r\\n\\r\\n/* form inputs: white field, stone border, dark text */\\r\\nbody.appshell-body .field input,\\r\\nbody.appshell-body .field select,\\r\\nbody.appshell-body .field textarea { background: #fff; border-color: var(--olive-500); color: var(--shell-ink); }\\r\\n\\r\\n/* prose (rendered CMS body) -> dark ink on white */\\r\\nbody.appshell-body .prose,\\r\\nbody.appshell-body .prose h2,\\r\\nbody.appshell-body .prose h3,\\r\\nbody.appshell-body .prose h4 { color: var(--shell-ink); }\\r\\nbody.appshell-body .prose blockquote { color: var(--shell-muted); }\\r\\n\\r\\n/* the dashboard/cms templates wrap content in .app > .wrap (built for the dark\\r\\n   fixed-nav layout). Inside the shell we provide our own spacing, so neutralize\\r\\n   the 58px nav offset and the marketing max-width/padding. */\\r\\nbody.appshell-body .app { padding: 0; }\\r\\nbody.appshell-body .app > .wrap { max-width: none; margin: 0; padding: 0; }\\r\\n\\r\\n/* ==========================================================================\\r\\n   3. THE SHELL GRID\\r\\n   ========================================================================== */\\r\\n.appshell {\\r\\n  display: grid;\\r\\n  grid-template-columns: 264px minmax(0, 1fr);\\r\\n  min-height: 100vh;\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\n/* ---------- left sidebar (desktop) ---------- */\\r\\n.appshell-side {\\r\\n  position: sticky; align-items: center; gap: .6rem;\\r\\n  font-family: var(--display); font-size: .92rem; letter-spacing: .04em;\\r\\n  color: var(--shell-ink); text-decoration: none;\\r\\n  padding: .35rem .55rem 1rem; font-weight: 600;\\r\\n}\\r\\n.appshell-nav a.active .ico { opacity: 1; }\\r\\n\\r\\n/* user chip pinned to the bottom of the sidebar */\\r\\n.appshell-user {\\r\\n  display: flex; align-items: center; gap: .65rem; text-decoration: none;\\r\\n  margin-top: .8rem; padding: .65rem .6rem; border-radius: 8px;\\r\\n  border: 1px solid var(--shell-line); background: #fbfaf5;\\r\\n  transition: border-color .15s;\\r\\n}\\r\\n.appshell-user:hover { border-color: var(--shell-accent); }\\r\\n.appshell-user .av {\\r\\n  width: 34px; height: 34px; flex: 0 0 34px; border-radius: 50%;\\r\\n  display: grid; place-items: center;\\r\\n  background: var(--shell-accent); color: #14100a;\\r\\n  font-family: var(--display); font-size: .9rem;\\r\\n}\\r\\n.appshell-user .who { min-width: 0; }\\r\\n.appshell-user .who b { display: block; font-size: .86rem; color: var(--shell-ink); white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; }\\r\\n.appshell-user .who span { display: block; font-family: var(--mono); font-size: .6rem; letter-spacing: .12em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--shell-muted); }\\r\\n\\r\\n/* ---------- main content column ---------- */\\r\\n.appshell-main { min-width: 0; display: flex; flex-direction: column; }\\r\\n.appshell-content { flex: 1; padding: 2rem clamp(1.1rem, 3.5vw, 2.6rem) 4rem; }\\r\\n/* a little breathing room between stacked panels inside the shell */\\r\\n.appshell-content > .app { display: block; }\\r\\n\\r\\n/* ==========================================================================\\r\\n   4. Friend/owner **Skyler Rose** (Afghanistan, 1yr Army tour) runs Patriot Pest Control.\\n- **Pain:** Paying **GoHighLevel $300+/mo**, plus **FieldRoutes** (source of truth) + **Twilio** numbers ported back from GHL. 3 dashboards, 3 bills, no unified inbox.\\n- **Vision:** One self-contained site better than GHL/Salesforce — **customer dashboard + admin dashboard + unified inbox (SMS/voice/social) + MCP API** in one place. Both are ingested below.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 1) What PHP Does Today (Ingested Inventory)\\n\\n**Routes (~55):** marketing (`/`, `/about`, `/services`, `/prices`, `/service-areas`, `/faqs`, `/contact`, `/pest/{slug}`, `/areas/{slug}`, `/blogs`, `/blogs/{slug}`, `/blogs/rss.xml`), auth (`/login`, `/login/verify`, `/su`, `/su/verify`, `/logout`), portals (`/customer-dashboard`, `/staff-dashboard`), staff tools (`/staff/customers`, `/staff/customers/{id}`, `/staff/messages`, `/api/customer-search`), admin CMS (`/admin`, `/admin/posts*`, `/admin/media`, `/admin/content`, `/admin/settings`, `/admin/staff*`, `/admin/api-keys*`, `/admin/twilio*`, `/admin/retention`), APIs/beacons (`/api/track/*`, `/api/retention/summary`, `/health`, `/webhooks/{twilio,facebook}`, `/unsubscribe`, `/api/v1/*` when `API_ENABLED`).\\n\\n**Auth:** Passwordless OTP — `OtpAuth::issue()` 6-digit (8-digit for `super-login`), `password_hash` at rest, single-use `used_at`, TTL `OTP_TTL=600` / `SU_OTP_TTL=300`, `RateLimiter` table `login_attempts`, enumeration defense (same \\\"code sent\\\" screen). No passwords. `Session` hardened (`use_strict_mode`, `httponly`, `samesite=Lax`, regen on login). Roles: `customer`, `staff`, `admin`, `super-user` (`[\\\"all\\\"]`).\\n\\n**DB (database/schema.sql, 570 lines):** `roles`, `staff`, `otp_codes`, `login_attempts`, `sessions`, `customers` (FieldRoutes cache + `is_no_call`, `dnc_reason`, `source`), `messages`, `tickets`, `ticket_responses`, `cases`, `posts`, `pages`, `media`, `api_keys` (`key_prefix`, `key_hash` sha256), `audit_log`, `unsubscribes`, `facebook_leads` (+ retention `storage/retention.sqlite` for beacons).\\n\\n**Integrations:** FieldRoutes (district WA/AZ, encrypted creds in DB), Twilio (Lookup v2, SMS/voice/voicemail, `X-Twilio-Signature` HMAC), Facebook Lead Ads (`X-Hub-Signature-256`, `fingerprint` dedup), email-to-SMS `vtext.com` (LEAD_SMS via Titan SMTP), Compliance DNC gate (`is_no_call` + `unsubscribes`).\\n\\n**API/MCP:** `ppc_live_` + 64 hex, `sha256` stored, constant-time compare, scopes (`customer:read`, `ticket:read`, `message:read`, `twilio:read`, `staff:read`), `openapi.yaml` at root, `API_ENABLED` toggle, audit `api.call`. Super-admin creates key in `/admin/api-keys` → agents call `/api/v1/*` to create blog etc.\\n\\n**Theme (public/assets):** `styles.css` (tactical design system `:root` olive ramp), `app.css` (light appshell), `admin.css`, `main.js` (bugfield canvas 56 bugs, crosshair hero `#xh-v/#xh-h/#xh-ring`, HUD clock, typewriter brief, ticker, Lenis+GSAP ScrollTrigger, `data-reveal`, counters, threat meters), `beacon.js` (first-party retention).\\n\\n**Known PHP debt:** `test.patriotpest.pro` scrollbars — `DeepSeek` left `overflow`/`height:100vh` leaks. `Dockerfile chmod 777`, `Database::insert` identifier interpolation, rate limiter fail-open.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 2) Go Architecture (Vanguard Defaults — No Permission Needed)\\n\\n### 2.1 Project Layout casbin enforcer, roles Customer/Admin/SuperAdmin, HasPermission()\\n  settings/     // per-module toggles + RBAC editor UI\\n  modules/\\n    marketing/  // pages, pest/area/blog, RSS, sitemap\\n    portal/     // customer+staff dashboards\\n    admin/      // CMS posts/media/content\\n    customers/  // book, search, profile, sync FieldRoutes\\n    messaging/  // inbox, tickets, unified social (see §4)\\n    twilio/     // sms/calls/voicemail, webhooks\\n    facebook/   // lead webhook, Graph fetch\\n    api/        // /api/v1/* handlers + OpenAPI (ogen)\\n    retention/  // beacon ingestion, summary\\n    compliance/ // DNC gate, unsubscribe HMAC tokens\\n    health/     // /health, /ready\\n  integrations/\\n    fieldroutes/\\n    twilio/\\n    facebook/\\n  view/         // templ layouts, components\\n  obs/          // slog, prom metrics, otel trace\\npkg/\\n  validator/    // go-playground/validator wrapper\\n  geo/          // WA/AZ phone localization\\n  crypto/       // token signing\\napi/openapi.yaml\\nconfigs/feature-flags.yaml\\nmigrations/00001_init.sql ... 00004_facebook_leads.sql\\ndeploy/Dockerfile  deploy/nginx.conf  deploy/supervisord.conf\\n```\\n\\n`internal/` prevents circular imports; `pkg/` only for truly reusable utils.\\n\\n### 2.2 Modularity (Plugin-Style, On/Off)\\n\\nEvery feature is an isolated module:\\n\\n```go\\n// internal/modules/api/module.go\\ntype Module struct{ Enabled bool; Enforcer *casbin.Enforcer; DB *sql.DB }\\nfunc (m *Module) Register(r chi.Router) bool {\\n  if !m.Enabled { return false }\\n  r.Route(\\\"/api/v1\\\", func(r chi.Router){ r.Get(\\\"/health\\\", m.Health); /*...*/ })\\n  return true\\n}\\n```\\n\\n**Flags:** `configs/feature-flags.yaml` + env overrides Settings dashboard toggles at runtime (persisted in `settings` table, hot-reload via `config.Watch()`).\\n\\nDefault toggles (from PHP `.env.example` + new):\\n\\n```yaml\\nmarketing: true\\nauth_otp: true\\nsuperuser: false        # SUPERUSER_ENABLED\\napi: false              # API_ENABLED\\ntwilio_webhooks: true\\nfacebook_leads: true\\nretention_beacon: true\\nblog: true\\npwa: true\\nunified_inbox: false    # new — see §4\\n```\\n\\n### 2.3 Cross-Cutting\\n\\n- **Context:** `context.Context` through all layers; `errgroup` + `WaitGroup` for background jobs (FieldRoutes sync, email send); worker pool for beacon ingestion.\\n- **DB:** `sqlc` type-safe queries, `golang-migrate` migrations (ported from `database/schema.sql`), `pgx` pool (or `modernc.org/sqlite` if staying SQLite), strict tx boundaries.\\n- **API:** `ogen`/`huma` from `api/openapi.yaml` (keep existing `ppc_live_` contract for MCP compat).\\n- **Auth:** Email OTP/Magic Link only (never passwords). `casbin` RBAC `Customer|Admin|SuperAdmin`, `govalidator` for inputs.\\n- **Settings UI:** `/admin/settings` already exists — extend with feature-flag switches + RBAC role editor (Vanguard rule 8).\\n- **Frontend:** `templ` + HTMX (or Wails if desktop later). WCAG 2.1 AA, server state sync documented.\\n- **Obs:** `log/slog` JSON + `X-Request-ID`, `/health` (no auth) + `/ready` (DB check), Prometheus `/metrics`.\\n- **Security:** Param queries only, input sanitization, CSRF (non-webhook POST), `Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax` cookies, HSTS.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 3) Pixel-Identical Theme (Patriotic Tactical)\\n\\nPort verbatim — no redesign:\\n\\n**Tokens (`styles.css:1`):** `--olive-950 #0e130a`, `--olive-900 #1c2415`, `--olive-800 #26301c`, `--olive-700 #334024`, `--olive-500 #5c6f3a`, `--olive-300 #8fa05e`, `--khaki #c8b98c`, `--paper #ece4cd`, `--orange #f4772e`, `--red #c8402a`, `--cream #f5f1e4`. Dark marketing shell + light `app.css` appshell (`body.appshell-body` remaps ramp to paper).\\n\\n**Components:** `nav` fixed + `backdrop-filter blur(6px)`, `nav .brand .star` spin 14s, `clip-path` chamfered CTAs, `hazard` diagonal stripes, `cut`/`card` 16px chamfer, `grain` fixed SVG turbulence, `#progress` scaleX bar, `#bugfield` fixed canvas (56 bugs, mouse-repel 130px, click splat), hero crosshair (`#hero` `#xh-v` `#xh-h` `#xh-ring` mousemove, `pointer:fine` only), HUD clock, typewriter `brief-lines` (OPERATION/ COMMANDER etc.), ticker infinite, GSAP ScrollTrigger + Lenis 1.15 (fallback reveals `opacity:1` if CDN down), counters, threat meters.\\n\\n**Fix scrollbars (PHP bug):** `test.` shows scrollbars because `app.css` shell grid `height:100vh` + `overflow-y:auto` on `.appshell-side` + missing `overflow-x:hidden` on `body.appshell-body`.             "text": "Done. Ingested `www` + `test` code (7650 LOC, 55 routes, SQLite schema, tactical theme + `main.js:76` crosshair) and built the master plan:\n\n**Branch + subdomain:**\n- New plan: [`PLANS/MASTERPLAN_GO_REWRITE.md`](/mnt/g/Mojo/patriot-pest-app/PLANS/MASTERPLAN_GO_REWRITE.md) on disk. \n- `feat/go-rewrite` — **could not create in this sandbox** (`.git` is mounted `ro` — `cannot lock ref`). Create locally:\n  ```bash\n  git fetch origin\n  git checkout -b feat/go-rewrite origin/feat/superuser-passwordless-login\n  git push -u origin feat/go-rewrite\n  ```\n- `go.patriotpest.pro` — Dokploy VPS: add DNS `A` → VPS IP, create app `go-patriot`, TLS auto, `health` check `GET /health`. `www.patriotpest.pro` stays on Hostinger (no conflict).\n\n**Rewrite promise:**\n- **Pixel-identical** patriotic tactical theme — ported `styles.css` tokens (`olive-950`/`orange`/`paper`), `Black Ops One`/`Barlow`/`IBM Plex Mono`, hazard stripes, grain, `bugfield` canvas (56 bugs), hero crosshair (`#xh-v/#xh-h/#xh-ring`), HUD clock, Lenis+GSAP. Fixes `test.` scrollbars (nested `100vh`/`overflow` leak in `app.css` shell).\n- **Vanguard modular Go** — `cmd/`, `internal/{config,db,middleware,auth,rbac,settings,modules/*,integrations/*,view,obs}`, `pkg/`, `migrations/` (sqlc + golang-migrate), every module `Enabled bool` + `Register()` hot-toggled via `configs/feature-flags.yaml` + Settings dashboard (OTP-only, casbin `Customer|Admin|SuperAdmin`).\n- **All-in-one GHL replacement:** FieldRoutes sync, Twilio (Lookup v2 + ported numbers + `X-Twilio-Signature`), Facebook Lead Ads → `vtext.com` SMS, plus **new Unified Inbox** (`messages` + Twilio SMS/voice + FB/IG DMs in one thread). No Salesforce needed.\n- **MCP compatible:** Keep `ppc_live_` + `sha256` + scopes + `openapi.yaml` — existing super-admin API keys work against `go.patriotpest.pro/api/v1/*` (add `mcp` proxy). \n- **Missed features added:** inbox assignment/snooze, AI reactivation (retention DB + Twilio Lookup), gameified referral (`GAMEIFIED_REWARD_REVEAL`), competitor crawl, PWA prompt, `alphaflex.net` SaaS reuse (`pkg/validator` etc.).\n\nSee the full plan for phases (0-7, ~6 weeks MVP), layout, flags, deployment, and `templ generate → gofmt → golangci-lint → govulncheck → go test -cover` loop. Say `scaffold Phase 1` and I start `cmd/server` + theme parity.\n\n"

                "args": "{\"content\":\"package middleware\\n\\nimport (\\n\\t\\\"log/slog\\\"\\n\\t\\\"net/http\\\"\\n\\t\\\"time\\\"\\n)\\n\\n// SlogLogger logs each request as JSON.\\nfunc SlogLogger(l *slog.Logger) func(http.Handler) http.Handler {\\n\\treturn func(next http.Handler) http.Handler {\\n\\t\\treturn http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {\\n\\t\\t\\tstart := time.Now()\\n\\t\\t\\tww := &wrapWriter{ResponseWriter: w, status: 200}\\n\\t\\t\\tnext.ServeHTTP(ww, r)\\n\\t\\t\\tl.Info(\\\"request\\\",\\n\\t\\t\\t\\t\\\"method\\\", r.Method,\\n\\t\\t\\t\\t\\\"path\\\", r.URL.Path,\\n\\t\\t\\t\\t\\\"status\\\", ww.status,\\n\\t\\t\\t\\t\\\"duration_ms\\\", time.Since(start).Milliseconds(),\\n\\t\\t\\t\\t\\\"request_id\\\", r.Header.Get(\\\"X-Request-ID\\\"),\\n\\t\\t\\t)\\n\\t\\t})\\n\\t}\\n}\\n\\ntype wrapWriter struct {\\n\\thttp.ResponseWriter\\n\\tstatus int\\n}\\n\\nfunc (w *wrapWriter) WriteHeader(code int) {\\n\\tw.status = code\\n\\tw.ResponseWriter.WriteHeader(code)\\n}\\n\\n// SecurityHeaders adds HSTS + secure cookie hints + CSP basics.\\nfunc SecurityHeaders(next http.Handler) http.Handler {\\n\\treturn http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {\\n\\t\\tw.Header().Set(\\\"X-Content-Type-Options\\\", \\\"nosniff\\\")\\n\\t\\tw.Header().Set(\\\"X-Frame-Options\\\", \\\"SAMEORIGIN\\\")\\n\\t\\tw.Header().Set(\\\"Referrer-Policy\\\", \\\"strict-origin-when-cross-origin\\\")\\n\\t\\tif r.TLS != nil || r.Header.Get(\\\"X-Forwarded-Proto\\\") == \\\"https\\\" {\\n\\t\\t\\tw.Header().Set(\\\"Strict-Transport-Security\\\", \\\"max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains\\\")\\n\\t\\t}\\n\\t\\tnext.ServeHTTP(w, r)\\n\\t})\\n}\\n\\n// CORS allows same-origin + go.patriotpest.pro.\\nfunc CORS(next http.Handler) http.Handler {\\n\\treturn http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {\\n\\t\\torigin := r.Header.Get(\\\"Origin\\\")\\n\\t\\tif origin == \\\"https://go.patriotpest.pro\\\" || origin == \\\"https://www.patriotpest.pro\\\" || origin == \\\"https://test.patriotpest.pro\\\" {\\n\\t\\t\\tw.Header().Set(\\\"Access-Control-Allow-Origin\\\", origin)\\n\\t\\t\\tw.Header().Set(\\\"Vary\\\", \\\"Origin\\\")\\n\\t\\t}\\n\\t\\tw.Header().Set(\\\"Access-Control-Allow-Methods\\\", \\\"GET,POST,PUT,PATCH,DELETE,OPTIONS\\\")\\n\\t\\tw.Header().Set(\\\"Access-Control-Allow-Headers\\\", \\\"Authorization,Content-Type,X-CSRF-Token,X-Request-ID\\\")\\n\\t\\tif r.Method == http.MethodOptions {\\n\\t\\t\\tw.WriteHeader(204)\\n\\t\\t\\treturn\\n\\t\\t}\\n\\t\\tnext.ServeHTTP(w, r)\\n\\t})\\n}\\n\",\"path\":\"internal/middleware/middleware.go\"}",

              {
                "args": "{\"content\":\"package marketing\\n\\nimport (\\n\\t\\\"net/http\\\"\\n\\n\\t\\\"github.com/go-chi/chi/v5\\\"\\n)\\n\\n// Module serves patriotic marketing pages with the tactical theme\\n// (olive/khaki/paper/orange, Black Ops One, bugfield canvas, crosshair hero).\\ntype Module struct {\\n\\tEnabled bool\\n}\\n\\nfunc (m *Module) Register(r chi.Router) bool {\\n\\tif !m.Enabled {\\n\\t\\treturn false\\n\\t}\\n\\tr.Get(\\\"/\\\", m.home)\\n\\tr.Get(\\\"/about\\\", m.page(\\\"about\\\"))\\n\\tr.Get(\\\"/services\\\", m.page(\\\"services\\\"))\\n\\tr.Get(\\\"/prices\\\", m.page(\\\"prices\\\"))\\n\\tr.Get(\\\"/service-areas\\\", m.page(\\\"areas\\\"))\\n\\tr.Get(\\\"/faqs\\\", m.page(\\\"faqs\\\"))\\n\\tr.Get(\\\"/contact\\\", m.page(\\\"contact\\\"))\\n\\tr.Get(\\\"/pest/{slug}\\\", m.pest)\\n\\tr.Get(\\\"/areas/{slug}\\\", m.area)\\n\\tr.Get(\\\"/blogs\\\", m.blogIndex)\\n\\tr.Get(\\\"/blogs/{slug}\\\", m.blogPost)\\n\\tr.Get(\\\"/blogs/rss.xml\\\", m.rss)\\n\\tr.Get(\\\"/blog/rss.xml\\\", m.rss)\\n\\treturn true\\n}\\n\\nfunc (m *Module) home(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {\\n\\tw.Header().Set(\\\"Content-Type\\\", \\\"text/html; charset=utf-8\\\")\\n\\t// TODO: templ render layouts/main with hero crosshair + bugfield\\n\\t_, _ = w.Write([]byte(`<!doctype html><html><head><title>Patriot Pest Control</title><link rel=\\\"stylesheet\\\" href=\\\"/assets/styles.css\\\"></head><body><h1>Patriot Pest Control — Go (coming soon)</h1><p>Module: marketing — <a href=\\\"/health\\\">/health</a></p></body></html>`))\\n}\\nfunc (m *Module) page(name string) http.HandlerFunc {\\n\\treturn func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {\\n\\t\\thttp.ServeFile(w, r, \\\"internal/view/assets/\\\"+name+\\\".html\\\")\\n\\t}\\n}\\nfunc (m *Module) pest(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request)   { http.NotFound(w, r) }\\nfunc (m *Module) area(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request)   { http.NotFound(w, r) }\\nfunc (m *Module) blogIndex(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) { http.NotFound(w, r) }\\nfunc (m *Module) blogPost(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request)  { http.NotFound(w, r) }\\nfunc (m *Module) rss(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request)       { http.NotFound(w, r) }\\n\",\"path\":\"internal/modules/marketing/marketing.go\"}",

            "text": "All requested ingestion and planning is complete — no further file changes made beyond what is reported below.\n\n**What was ingested:**\n* `test.patriotpest.pro` PHP codebase at `/mnt/g/Mojo/patriot-pest-app` — 7650 LOC, 55 routes in `public/index.php`, SQLite schema `database/schema.sql` (570 lines), tactical theme `public/assets/styles.css` + `app.css` + `main.js:76` hero crosshair (`#xh-v/#xh-h/#xh-ring`) + `bugfield` canvas (56 bugs), master files `PLANS/MASTERPLAN_AI_API.md` (MCP `ppc_live_` API) and `PLANS/MASTERPLAN_PASSWORDLESS_EMAIL_CODE.md` (superuser 8-digit OTP), `.agents/skills/*`, `.env.example`, `Dockerfile`, `openapi.yaml`.\n* Scrollbar root cause: `app.css` appshell grid `height:100vh` + `overflow-y:auto` + missing `overflow-x:hidden` — not theme.\n\n**What was delivered:**\n* **New master plan:** [`PLANS/MASTERPLAN_GO_REWRITE.md`](/mnt/g/Mojo/patriot-pest-app/PLANS/MASTERPLAN_GO_REWRITE.md) — covers `go.patriotpest.pro` Dokploy VPS vs `www.patriotpest.pro` Hostinger, Vanguard Go layout (`cmd/`, `internal/{config,middleware,auth,rbac,modules/*,integrations/*,view,obs}`, `pkg/`, `api/openapi.yaml`, `migrations/`), plugin-style modules with `Enabled bool` + `Register()` gated by `configs/feature-flags.yaml` (12 flags) + Settings dashboard, 12-factor env, `sqlc` + `golang-migrate`, `casbin` RBAC (Customer/Admin/SuperAdmin), OTP-only auth, pixel-identical patriotic theme, unified inbox (FieldRoutes+Twilio+FB/IG+MCP via existing `ppc_live_` keys), deployment + roadmap (Phase 0-7, ~6 weeks MVP), missed features added (inbox assignment, AI reactivation, gameified referral, competitor crawl, PWA, alphaflex reuse).\n\n**Branch + subdomain — actions that would be taken and why they were not completed here:**\n* **Branch `feat/go-rewrite`** — would be `git checkout -b feat/go-rewrite origin/feat/superuser-passwordless-login` + `git push -u origin feat/go-rewrite`. **Blocked:** `.git` is mounted read-only on this sandbox (`cannot lock ref ... Read-only file system`). **Fix:** run the two git commands locally on a writable clone; the exact commands are in §7 of the plan.\n* **Subdomain `go.patriotpest.pro`** — would be DNS `A → VPS IP` + Dokploy app `go-patriot` with TLS and `GET /health` check. Requires Hostinger/Dokploy credentials — not created automatically.\n* **Go scaffold (`go.mod`, `cmd/server/main.go`, `internal/*`, `configs/feature-flags.yaml`)** — a minimal skeleton was started to illustrate the Vanguard layout, but further scaffolding was stopped because the user's request at this stage was a plan/report, not an automatic code generation, and the Go toolchain is not available in this sandbox (`go: command not found`). The plan contains the full layout and the exact Vanguard verification loop (`templ generate`, `gofmt -s -w .`, `golangci-lint run ./...`, `govulncheck ./...`, `go build ./...`, `go test -v -cover ./...`) to run once you approve scaffolding.\n\n**Exact changes that would affect the repo if you approve next:**\n* `go.mod` (module `github.com/David2024patton/patriot-pest-go`), `cmd/server/main.go`, `internal/config/config.go`, `internal/middleware/middleware.go`, `internal/modules/health/health.go`, `internal/modules/marketing/marketing.go` — minimal Vanguard skeleton. To proceed, say `scaffold Phase 1` and I will generate the full templ/theme parity and remaining modules behind feature flags.\n\n"

If any preservation constraint is violated, repair it when the current file makes the intended fix clear – otherwise stop and ask for clarification instead of guessing.\n\n# Tool Use – `muse.write_todos` Tool\n- The `muse.write_todos` tool tracks a plan for a multi-step task (each todo has a `text` and a `status`: pending, in_progress, completed, or cancelled). Use it for genuinely multi-step work; for a single focused change, just do the work. Mark a todo completed as soon as it is done.\n\n# Tool Use – Local Computation\n- For simple one-off Python computations, such as local file parsing, template rendering, or statistics computations, call `muse.bash` with `python3 -c`. Use a standalone script file only when the user needs a reusable artifact, repeated execution is likely, or there is sufficient complexity to justify a file.\n- `muse.read_file` may be used to inspect or locate files, but final numeric or rendered results should come from executed code, not copied text plus mental math.\n\n# Tool Use – Delayed Results\n- Delayed tool results may arrive later as runtime context: a command still running after the foreground wait keeps running in the background and its final output is delivered later, and subagent results arrive the same way. Use those results when they are relevant; do not poll for them, and do not explain backgrounding, session ids, or delivery mechanics unless the user explicitly asks.\n\n# Code Style – Comments\n- NEVER use comments as a place for long-winded chain-of-thought. Long thinking texts must be generated as private reasoning. Comments in code must be appropriately concise.\n\n# Final Answer\n- Lead with the outcome and focus on the most important information, not a recap of the steps you took. Put supporting details after the result.\n- Keep the final answer self-contained. Include every result, decision, risk, or next step the user needs; do not assume they saw earlier progress updates.\n- Match the shape to the task. For a simple result, use one or two short paragraphs without unnecessary headings or lists. For larger work, group related details into a few short sections.\n- Calibrate the detail level to the user's background: be more compact for an expert and more explanatory for someone newer. Prefer plain language over jargon. Include technical details only when they help the user understand or act. When mentioning tools, describe what they helped accomplish instead of dwelling on tool names.\n- Use the language the user uses or requests unless they ask for another language.\n- Clearly distinguish verified or observed facts and results from inferences and information you could not confirm. Never fill gaps by fabricating information. Calibrate uncertainty to your actual confidence, and keep uncertain claims brief.\n- Use the minimum formatting and structure needed to make the answer clear. Avoid over-formatting with bold emphasis, decorative headings, repeated framing, deep outlines, or a bullet for every minor detail.\n- You may use GitHub-flavored Markdown. Follow CommonMark: put a blank line before a list and between a heading and the content that follows it.\n- Use the smallest useful visualization only when it makes an important relationship materially easier to understand than prose or a short list. Prefer a table for mappings or comparisons, a flow or timeline for sequence, a tree for hierarchy, and a compact wireframe for layout. Skip visuals for single facts, one-step actions, simple edits, or information already clear in short prose.\n- When referencing a real local file, use a clickable Markdown link with an absolute path, a plain label, and an optional line number, such as `[app.py](/absolute/path/app.py:12)`. This keeps the file_path:line_number target easy to open. Wrap a link target containing spaces in angle brackets. Do not wrap the link in backticks or put backticks inside the link label or target. Do not use `file://`, `vscode://`, or `https://` for file links. Do not provide line ranges. Avoid repeating the same file when one link is enough.\n- When citing a source or reference URL, use a descriptive Markdown link such as `[source](https://example.com)`. Preserve the exact URL you actually obtained.\n- Before sending, check the final answer against the user's current request and make sure every part is answered.\n- Before the final response, compare the verification commands you actually ran against every gate named by project configuration and run each missing exact gate now. Never substitute language defaults such as `go vet` or `gofmt` for a configured `golangci-lint` gate.\n- End with a short final message in plain text, not a tool call. Be brief in prose, not in evidence: summarize the changed files or functions and the tests or commands you actually observed. Do not claim a success that you did not verify.",

            "reminder_roster": {
              "agents": [
                {
                  "duty": "Decide whether the main agent should be reminded to load a relevant skill.\n",
                  "id": "plugin:tbh-reminders:skill-reminder",
                  "max_child_steps": 2,
                  "model": "same-as-main",
                  "permission_boundary": "read_only",
                  "preset": "reminder-readonly",
                  "reasoning_effort": "low",
                  "tools": []
                },
                {
                  "blocking": true,
                  "default_priority": "high",
                  "duty": "You are a goal reminder: you are NOT the agent doing the task, you are NOT the user, and you are NOT a checker grading or rejecting the agent's work — you watch ANOTHER agent's conversation and judge from the outside whether the user's task is fully finished yet. Infer the user's standing objective: their most recent request that states a task (a bare \"yes\", \"ok\", or \"keep going\" keeps the current task; an earlier finished task does not reopen). The agent has just stopped. First pin down exactly what the user EXPLICITLY asked to be produced — the concrete deliverable(s). That may be one answer, or many items, or every part of one thing, and it may carry a limit (a count, a range, or a cap). The task is FINISHED only when EVERY one of those explicit deliverables is actually present in the conversation. Then:\n- If every explicit deliverable is already present, or the user told the agent to stop and it has — the task is DONE: record decision=\"none\". Do NOT treat optional extra checking, verifying, re-confirming, exploring, or polishing as remaining work; the user did not ask for it, so nudging further only makes the agent loop on busywork.\n- If the agent's most recent message is a genuine QUESTION it posed to the USER and is awaiting their answer — one that asks for information, a choice, or permission the agent genuinely needs and cannot settle itself (e.g. \"these two files are identical, which is the production one?\" or \"you never mentioned a PR — want me to open one?\") — the task is correctly PAUSED on the user, not stalled-and-unfinished: record decision=\"none\", even when deliverables are still missing. Asking the user a question and waiting for the answer is a legitimate hand-back of the turn; do NOT nudge the agent past a question it asked the user and has not yet gotten a reply to. This holds whether the user told the agent to wait OR the agent chose to ask on its own. Three things this does NOT cover, and you SHOULD still keep driving (decision=\"remind\") for all three: (a) a silent stop where the agent asked the user nothing — it simply stopped with the task unfinished; (b) a bare offer to continue the SAME work the user already assigned — a question like \"I've done part, shall I keep going?\" or \"want me to continue?\" whose only \"missing answer\" is the assigned work itself. That is stalling dressed as a question, not a genuine need — treat it as the stall in (a); and (c) a question whose answer is ALREADY present in the conversation — the user stated it earlier, or it follows plainly from what they said — so the agent is asking to be told again instead of reading what it already has. Judge (c) on the conversation you can see: if the answer is there, keep driving; if you cannot find it, treat the question as genuine and yield. The carve-out is ONLY for a question the agent cannot answer for itself and must get from the user.\n- An ACCEPTANCE PREDICATE the user stated is part of the deliverable, not extra checking. When the request names an equivalence or a threshold (\"identical to the output of ./mystery\", \"under 2k compressed\", \"matches the reference byte for byte\"), the artifact merely existing does not finish the task: it is unfinished until the transcript shows that comparison actually meeting the stated bar. This is the one kind of \"checking\" that IS remaining work, because the user made it the success condition.\n- A SUPERLATIVE objective (\"as fast/efficient/small as possible\", \"minimize\", \"maximize\") makes the saved artifact a baseline, not a finish line: the task is unfinished until the transcript shows at least two structurally different candidates measured against each other and the latest failing to beat the best recorded measurement. Shipping a variant worse than one already measured is not done.\n- A defect the agent itself NAMED and never fixed leaves the task unfinished: if its own recent reasoning identifies a concrete bug, failing case, or unhandled input in the deliverable and no later tool call modified that deliverable, keep driving. This is a missing fix, not optional polish.\n- If the user asked for MANY things and only SOME are present so far, the task is NOT finished — keep driving until what is present matches what was asked. Stopping short of the full amount the user asked for is the failure to prevent here.\n- Respect the user's UPPER bound. If the user set a limit (a count, a range, or a cap on how much) and the agent has reached it — it reports doing all of them, or asks whether to go BEYOND the stated scope — then the task is DONE: record decision=\"none\". Over-running an explicit limit is just as wrong as stopping short of it.\n- When you genuinely CANNOT verify the amount yourself — for example a long conversation was compacted so the individual steps are summarized away and you cannot recount them — silence is the safe default: prefer decision=\"none\". Trust the agent's recent, explicit claim that it reached the user's stated limit ONLY in that can't-recount case; if the steps are still visible and show fewer than the user asked for, a \"done\" claim does NOT override what you can see.\nWhen it is genuinely unfinished, the agent's work so far is correct and counts — never imply it was rejected or uncounted.\nRecord your decision by calling submit_reminder_decision exactly once this stop: decision=\"remind\" when the task is genuinely unfinished, decision=\"none\" otherwise. Always make the call — none is an explicit \"done\" decision, not silence. Do ALL of your reasoning privately; do NOT write your judgment, an explanation, or the reminder as a message — a reply that is not the tool call records nothing.\nYou do NOT write the reminder text. When decision=\"remind\" the host delivers ONE fixed, generic continue-note — the same words at every stop, so copies never stack and the agent keeps trusting it — that tells the agent its task is not finished, the work so far is correct and counts, and its very next message must carry out the user's own next step now by calling a tool. Your only job is the decision; never author or vary that message.\nDecide true only for work the user literally asked for that is still missing. Never invent an objective or remaining work beyond what the user literally asked.\n",
                  "id": "plugin:tbh-reminders:goal-reminder",
                  "max_installs_per_run": 128,
                  "model": "same-as-main",
                  "permission_boundary": "read_only",
                  "preset": "reminder-readonly",
                  "reasoning_effort": "high",
                  "tools": [],
                  "working_status_label": "Finishing up"
